title: Hero rating rule (BC Calculate Rating): gear outside base profile/options adds rating only when Attacks+Wounds >= 3; recalculate all gear at that moment; armour upgrade outside options +1 until then; warriors use option points
description: Read the BC rulebook section; replace the +5 per stage guess; tests; REVIEW notes. Also check whether any beast can promote to hero and report; beasts get armour upgrades only via options or hero pool.
notes: Done. BC 'Step 4: Calculate Ratings' implemented as written: gear in the base profile or the profile's Options: no adjustment; other gear/equipment: Armoury/Equipment rating, warrior column below Attacks+Wounds 3, hero column from 3, recomputed every build; armour upgrade: stages above max(profile armour, armour in Options) x (1 below 3, 5 from 3) (replaces the +5 guess); warriors: option points (OptionsCover). Tests hero_rating_test.go, armour_test.go. BEASTS: Hero-capable beasts exist: Wild Warg (Angmar, Mirkwood), Isengard Warg (Wolves of Isengard), Fell Warg (Dol Guldur) are not On Their Own Path and may lead/Hero in the Making; Cirith Ungol's Mirkwood Giant Spider is not own-path either (but cannot lead, StartHeroes). All other beasts (Werewolf, Crebain, spiders of Mirkwood/Dol Guldur, War Drake, War Bat) are On Their Own Path and never become heroes. Armour upgrades: a Beast warrior now only through its profile's options; once a hero, through the hero pool. IRON HILLS SPEAR: chart row 'Iron Hills Warrior (Spear)' is a warrior with only the Spear of the option 'Shield and Spear' (2 points as bundle). Today priced 10 + 2 = 12: OptionsCover charges the cheapest option that contains the leftover item (the whole bundle). Before the price rule it was 11 (10 + the Spear's armoury rating 1). BC text: 'Warrior models may only spend influence in order to match one of their profile's Options' and 'A Warrior may drop Wargear provided it keeps a legal Option, or buys a new legal Option' so a lone Spear is not a legal Option; the BC document says nothing about taking part of a bundle, and 'Warriors are worth the same points as in MESBG'. Options for the user: keep 12 (bundle price, nothing dropped), 11 (rating), or make the row 'Shield, Spear' (2).

title: Live match mode: spec (domain expert) for matches rework
description: See the user's description recorded in the notes of this bead: match start rules, locked company, Retreated and Field casualties zones, wound/might/will/fate trackers, action trackers (wounded unit, passed fate roll, broken courage roll, retreated, died, mount removed/re-added), undo with match log, live sync to other players viewing the company page. Expert writes docs/ spec + split beads (backend planner for sync design: recommend SSE/websocket).
notes:
USER SPEC: LIVE MATCH MODE (2026-10-21)
Once a match starts (a match can only be created if all other participants are not already in a running match), the My company page changes radically:
- We are no longer between matches (technically in or after the aftermath; at campaign start it is a little weird because there are no matches).
- Cannot change the company's gear, recruit units or modify it permanently until the match is over.
- Two new zones between the "Battle company" and "Cemetery" sections: Retreated (units that retreat during the match) and Field casualties (units "killed", wounds at 0, which must roll for injuries in the aftermath).
- Unit cards get match trackers (only exist during the match): the Wounds attribute becomes a wound counter (lowered by enemy units declaring a wound against your unit, or manually for any other reason; zero marks the unit a casualty for the match); Might, Will and Fate become trackers that can be lowered and increased.
- Action trackers (change the status of the unit or another unit, and give xp after the match per the rules):
  * Wounded a unit: prompted for the number of wounds, to which units (and/or their mounts) and how many wounds were resisted. Check the rules on wounding and killing: I believe only the first wound gives xp and only the first kill gives xp, except killing heroes which always awards xp.
  * Passed a fate roll (lowers the fate tracker automatically).
  * Passed a Broken company courage roll (first time awards xp).
  * Retreated: failed a courage roll or exited the battlefield; no injury roll; removed from the active part of the page, cannot do anything or be targeted from the match; moves to Retreated.
  * Died: when not due to an enemy injury.
  * The mount can be removed to indicate the unit fell and is now infantry; gear requiring a mount (lances) and associated keywords are struck through. The mount can be re-added in case of error.
  * All trackers are revertible; all tracker changes are recorded in a match log; undoing an action removes it from the log.
- Ideally the companies' pages involved in a live match are synced with the other players via "webhooks" (live push) so they see changes as they happen without reloading, without being able to modify trackers (not their company). E.g. I mark a unit retreated, the card moves to Retreated, and another player viewing my company page sees it live.
- A company not in match mode needs no live sync: plain page as now.
Spec done: docs/live-match.md (commit cdc1e05). XP answer: woundedEnemy/fatePrevented/brokenCourage are once-only flags; slainHeroOrMonster counts every Hero/Monster kill; killing warriors gives nothing. Implementer beads created under pib (db, backend x4, curator, frontend x7) and question beads q1-q3. REVIEW defaults listed at the end of the doc.

title: Armoury: Minas Tirith can buy pikes and elf bows although not available to them (items matched by stats/class, not identity)
description: Two causes suspected: (1) Elf bow and Longbow treated as the same item since same stats; faction flavour must be kept (related, not identical); (2) Pike and Spear treated as identical; the Pike is two-handed, supports like a spear and also allows support through a second pike-bearer (pike chain). Find where identity/availability is resolved (gear annotations classes, armoury availability, limits) and make availability per item name/faction.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (curator 2026-10-20): same price-group collapse (see rzt.2) plus two matching bugs in internal/core/battlecompanies.go GearMatchesOption: (a) it matches an option text with strings.Contains(option, itemName or alias), so 'spear' is found inside 'war spear', 'throwing spears', 'troll spear', 'elven spear' and 'bow' inside 'crossbow', 'longbow', 'elf bow'; and an offer 'Pike' with alias 'Spear' matches the Minas Tirith option 'Shield and Spear'; (b) a class fallback (EquipSpear words spear/pike, EquipBow word bow, EquipShield word shield) treats every item of a class as the same item when it has a single class. shop.whyNot 'Already carried' also compares aliases, so a Spear blocks a Pike. Fix: offers per exact item (identity = normalised name or true synonym alias from gearAnnotations), option parsed into item parts and compared by identity; no class fallback; item relations recorded as data (relatedTo).
FIXED (core): GearMatchesOption now compares item identity (internal/core/gearidentity.go ItemKey/OptionItems). Warrior of Minas Tirith may buy exactly Bow, Spear, Shield (test). Pike, Elf Bow, Longbow, Crossbow, Light Shield no longer offered; Elven-made weapons (Elven pike/spear/lance/throwing/hand-and-a-half) are their own offers at the generic price (BC table footnote), available through the unit option. Heroes: any item of their company's profiles (unchanged rule, now exact). Pike data: two-handed, supports like a spear and through a second pike (ability support depth 2, twoHanded, duel penalty with shield/missile). REVIEW: Wood Elf Spear and Elven Glaive are not priced via the generic table (no rule says so); a Mattock for a Mordor Uruk-hai (option 'Two-handed weapon') is no longer offered (identity).
FIXED with rzt.13 (empty-options bug in legalWargear) plus earlier identity work; table tests over all 37 companies. REVIEW: Mattock vs 'Two-handed weapon' option kept distinct.

title: Gear tooltips resolve the wrong item: spear shows pike, shield shows light shield, longbow shows crossbow (company chooser page)
description: Minas Tirith and others. Tooltips must show the item's own text. A bow-type weapon (Longbow, Elf bow) lets the unit move up to half its move and shoot with a penalty; a crossbow needs the unit still; check crossbow strength (user thinks S4). Likely name matching/aliases or class-based lookup in the tooltip code; fix root cause.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (curator 2026-10-20): the BC wargear table (data.wargear.items[].names) lists PRICE GROUPS (Pike/Spear/Lance/Warspear; Light Shield/Shield; Elf Bow/Esgaroth Bow/Longbow/Dwarf Longbow/Crossbow). Two Go consumers collapse a group into ONE item named after names[0] with the rest as aliases: (1) internal/core/glossary_extras.go gearTerm() makes one glossary term per group (add(names[0],..., names[1:]...)); in glossary.go the BC extra REPLACES the file's term of the first name and registers the others as its aliases, so owner['spear'] -> 'Pike' term, 'shield' -> 'Light Shield' term, 'longbow' -> 'Elf Bow' term etc.; the chip tooltip (internal/web/companies.go Named -> glossary.Find) then shows the wrong text. (2) battlecompanies.go Armoury(): one GearOffer per group, Name=names[0], AlsoCalled=rest. Fix: one item per name everywhere, text from data.gearAnnotations[name].definition. Data: gearAnnotations already has one entry per item with its own text; the BC glossary terms must come from those, not from price groups. Crossbow is S4 in BC annotations (derived from vanilla) - verified in vanilla/BC sources, see child bead.

FE (frontend-implementer): no web-side cause: chip tooltips show what glossary.Find returns (core). Nothing to do in web until rzt.10 lands; recheck chooser tooltips then.
FIXED (data+core, curator): chips on the company chooser page use rs.Glossary.Find(name); now each wargear name has its own glossary term (rulebook term when the glossary file has one: Spear, Pike, Shield->Shields, Light Shield, Bow, Crossbow; otherwise a term built from data.gearAnnotations[name].definition: Longbow, Elf Bow...). No web change needed. FOR FRONTEND (optional, better): for gear chips prefer rs.BC.Annotation(name) -> Definition (item's own text incl. move-and-shoot rule), Stats(), Related []string (related but distinct items, e.g. Elf Bow <-> Longbow), and wargear lists now carry resolved names (data.wargearReadAs: Rivendell 'spear' -> 'Elven spear', Mordor Orc 'bow' -> 'Orc bow', Dwarf 'two-handed axe' -> 'Two-handed weapon'). REVIEW: those four readings are curator guesses, user to confirm. Crossbow is S4 (24in) in vanilla, BC annotations and the rulebook chart.
FE verified in browser: chooser chips and glossary give each item its own text (Spear, Pike, Light Shield, Longbow, Elf Bow, Crossbow: cannot fire after moving, 4 Strength in the armoury; bows: shoot after moving up to half Move at -1). The chip for plain 'shield' links the vanilla 'Shields' term (correct). Armoury shows one entry per item.

title: Poison is a unit rule: plain wargear, Poisoned Attacks (<weapon>) on the unit, Envenom Weapon chooses a weapon
description:
OWNER DESIGN 2026-10-27. Data done by the curator (docs/definitions.md '**Poison**'); this bead is the Go side.

DATA NOW
- The item 'Bow with poisoned arrows' and the 'poisoned' modifier no longer exist (no variantOf, no grantsModifier). Harad rows read 'bow with poisoned arrows' / 'bow with poison arrows' as the plain 'Bow' (data.wargearReadAs, 3 readings); the Haradrim Warrior and Raider profiles already carry Poisoned Attacks (Bow)/(bow) in vanilla, so the unit is poisonous without any grant.
- Blowpipe is the only item that itself grants a rule: grants ['Poisoned Attacks (Blowpipe)'] (unchanged).
- Envenom Weapon (X) annotation: weaponModifier true, grants ['Poisoned Attacks (X)'], NEW grantsRuleForChosenWeapon {rule:'Poisoned Attacks', weaponClasses:[melee,two_handed,spear,lance,bow,crossbow,throwing,missile]}. Contract: the player chooses ONE item of the unit whose class is in weaponClasses and that is not already named by a held Poisoned Attacks (<weapon>) rule; the UNIT gains the rule 'Poisoned Attacks (<weapon name>)'; the weapon stays plain. Today's Equipment.Modifies/Detail store the choice (keep). Load grantsRuleForChosenWeapon in GearAnnotation (battlecompanies.go) and use weaponClasses instead of the hard-coded melee/two-handed/spear/lance list in companybuild.go (~l.202; Envenom today cannot pick a bow or a thrown weapon) and isWeapon in levelling.go.

BACKEND TO DO
1. Unit rules come from the profile + items' grants + chosen-weapon grants: an Envenom Weapon with a chosen weapon adds UnitRule 'Poisoned Attacks (<weapon>)' (source Envenom Weapon). A level-up Poisoned Attacks|weapon:<name> gives the same rule (already).
2. PROMOTION: the rule is a UNIT rule. A promotion keeps the plain weapon (judged by item identity as now) but NOT the poison unless the new profile has the rule itself (Haradrim Warrior -> Raider keeps it because both profiles have it). Blowpipe: item and its grant leave together. Envenom Weapon (equipment) stays; if the new profile no longer lists the chosen weapon, its rule is dropped and Modifies is cleared (or the player re-chooses; ask the owner if re-choice is wanted).
3. Dedupe: a unit with Poisoned Attacks (Blowpipe) from profile AND item shows it once.
4. FAILING TESTS TO UPDATE (they encode the old item): internal/core/gearmodifiers_test.go:21 (TestItemModifiersExplainedInTheTooltip uses 'Bow with poisoned arrows'; use the Elven spear only) and internal/core/promotion_gear_test.go:45 (case 'a bow with poisoned arrows is a Bow': use a plain Bow; assert the Haradrim Raider keeps Bow and still has Poisoned Attacks (Bow) from its profile). Add a test: promotion Haradrim Warrior (Bow) -> a profile without the rule keeps Bow, no poison.
5. Related owner decisions kept: 'Two-handed axe' = 'Two-handed weapon' alias; different weapons are different items; Khandish exchange-label rule is for the backend.
TTS: golden already regenerated (the Harad rows now emit option 'Bow', no optionDropped notes).
notes: DONE (Go side). Commits: test(core) poison tests; refactor(core) promotion per-item + no variantOf + loads grantsRuleForChosenWeapon; feat(core) Envenom Weapon; web chooser. DESIGN: the chosen weapon is stored in the bought item's name ('Envenom Weapon (X)' = none yet, 'Envenom Weapon (Bow)' = chosen; BCBook.ChosenWeapon resolves it for Annotation/Offer) because UnitState has no field and the DB maps explicit columns (no schema change). Earlier code auto-picked the first melee weapon; now an unchosen modifier gives no rule until the player chooses. One function (applyWeaponModifiers/CanBePoisoned, poison.go) lists eligible weapons for BOTH Envenom and the level-up minor rule (HeroSheet.Weapons = CompanyUnit.PoisonableWeapons). ArmouryService.BuyEquipmentFor(...,weapon) and ChooseModifierWeapon(unit, modifier, weapon). Web: weapon_chooser partial in buy window and expanded card, route POST .../equipment/weapon. REMAINING for frontend: the Armory-tab buy form (handleArmoryBuy) does not ask for the weapon (item is bought pending, then chosen on the card). REVIEW: promotion that loses the chosen weapon resets to 'Envenom Weapon (X)' and the player may choose again among the new weapons (owner question open). REVIEW: unchosen Envenom gives no rule (was: silently the first melee weapon). REVIEW: Khandish exchange label becomes the new profile's own wargear / matching exchange option; no stored duplicate. OPEN: VariantOf field is dead code now (GearOffer/Equipment/GearAnnotation, GearMatchesOption); schema still declares variantOf: no data uses it.

description: Owner request: audit Go code for whole-app-down/wedge errors beyond net/http recover. Chunks recorded as notes.

Chunk1 FIXED (HIGH): goroutines in core/rules.go (rule set build; panic in parser killed process and left waiters hanging) and cmd/server live hub Start (feed/callback panic) now recovered via core.safely; hub restarts feed after 1s. Chunk2/3 FIXED: http.Server had only ReadHeaderTimeout (slowloris on body, idle conns forever): added Read 60s/Write 120s/Idle 120s/MaxHeaderBytes 64K; SSE verified to survive (per-write deadlines; test). limitBody middleware: 1 MiB cap for non-multipart bodies (net/http default was 10 MB urlencoded per request); multipart handlers keep own limits (handlers.go, admin.go, glossary.go). recoverer now logs stack+path and re-panics ErrAbortHandler. title: Officer succession: replace a dead Sergeant and use the Warrior fallback for Sergeants
description: Rule (BC rulebook, Death of a Hero): 'If you ever have less than two Sergeants, another Hero ... who is not already a Leader or Sergeant, may become a Sergeant.' and 'Should you not have another Hero model available to replace a Leader or Sergeant who has died, then the Warrior with the most Experience Points is instantly treated as having rolled Hero in the Making' (ties: highest Rating, then player). See docs/definitions.md 'Officer succession'. App gaps in internal/core/aftermath_service.go successionOpen/decideSuccession and aftermath.go NextSuccession/NextSergeant: (1) successionOpen returns nil unless rec.Work.LeaderFell, so a Sergeant who dies or retires while the Leader lives never triggers a replacement; (2) NextSergeant sets NeedSergeant only if a non-officer Hero exists, so with no Hero left a lost Sergeant gets no Warrior-with-most-XP fallback (only the Leader does). Fix: set a SergeantFell/officerLost flag in advance (wasLeader analogue) for Sergeants, open a Sergeant question when fewer than two Sergeants (options = Heroes, else Fallback = mostExperienced warriors, ties by Rating then player; fallback Warrior gets HeroBonus(nil) and chooses its path as for the Leader); keep the Sergeant place optional when Heroes exist. Update docs/aftermath.md. Matches the rule already: Hero first then Warrior for the Leader; displaced officers (Ranger of the North) stay Heroes.

title: Unbuilt rules 3: company Break Point in play, Broken company and All is Lost in the BC json
description: Formalise campaign.breakPoint (percent, counting, evaluation, effects when Broken, Stand Fast, scenario exceptions, All is Lost, experience gain), schema, validator, docs.
notes:
SPEC (curator, 2026-10-21). Data: campaign.breakPoint (new), companies[].effects[kind=breakPoint].percent (existing: only Muster of Isengard 66), campaign.influence.allIsLost (text, now points to campaign.breakPoint.allIsLost), campaign.experience.gains[key=brokenCourageTestPassed] (existing), matchInput.perCompany startingModels / brokenAtTurn / fledBroken. Schema + validator + docs done.

SOURCES: BC doc never defines 'Broken'; it uses the Rules Manual: Broken Army (46): Break Point is half the models in the starting Army, not rounded (13 -> 6.5), never changes; 'If, at the start of any turn, the number of casualties ... is greater than its Break Point, then your Army is considered to be Broken from that point onwards'; every Activation a model takes a Courage Test before doing anything else; engaged/unable to activate models do not test; fail = flees and is removed as a casualty. Stand Fast (47): Hero that passes calls Stand Fast at end of activation; friendly Warriors activating within 6" with LoS auto-pass; other Heroes test. Cavalry and Break Points: rider's death is the casualty; mount's alone is not. Chariot: automatically passes. Heroic Resolve: auto-pass for a Hero (BC Mastery: without Might if Broken). BC: 'Muster of Isengard: Break Point is 66% rather than 50%.' All is Lost!: 'Any Battle Company may choose to voluntarily flee the battlefield once their force is broken. This is decided at the beginning of the turn that they're broken and before priority. Their opponent claims victory and full rewards ... The fleeing company earns the standard amount of Influence points for participating, but nothing further.' Experience: '+1 for Rolling for and then passing a Courage test for being Broken.' Scenario rules: Defend the Hill (models on the hill no tests), Let nothing through! (Defender auto-pass within 6" of the Gate), Only a Pony After All (Baggage Ponies do not count towards the Defender's Break Point), Neutral Third-Party (no tests), Maelstrom of Battle (models yet to arrive count as on the battlefield). Broken Honour Hero: no Stand Fast; Wanderers: no Stand Fast.

INTERPRETATION (data shape, exact): see campaign.breakPoint. Key facts:
- Break Point = percent (company effect or default 50) x startingModels / 100, not rounded. Broken iff casualties * 100 > percent * startingModels, evaluated at the START of each turn only, permanent.
- startingModels = models of the company in the starting force: Warriors, Heroes, creatures (they are models on the board; the Baggage Pony exception implies they count), the temporary Wanderer, models yet to arrive; NOT neutral models; a composite model (Warg Marauder card, 3 riders + mount) counts per physical model (see REVIEW). Cavalry = one model, Chariot one, War Beast + Commander two.
- casualties = models removed as casualties, including models that fled after failing a Broken courage test (they leave 'as a casualty'); a Cavalry rider's death counts, the mount's alone not. Models that left through a scenario rule (escaped) are not casualties (REVIEW).
- Effects when Broken: Courage test (2d6 >= Courage) at every activation before anything else; exempt: engaged, unable to activate; auto-pass: Stand Fast, Heroic Resolve, Chariot, scenarioExceptions; fail: flees = removed as casualty (and 'fled' in matchInput, no injury roll). Passing Hero calls Stand Fast (6", LoS) unless Broken Honour or Wanderer.
- All is Lost: offered once, at the start of the turn the company becomes Broken, before Priority; opponent victory + full scenario rewards; fleeing company only the participation Influence (campaign.influence.gains.participating). matchInput.fledBroken feeds it.
- Experience: brokenCourageTestPassed is +1 once per model per match, only when the model ROLLED the test and passed (any number of passes = 1). Automatic passes (Stand Fast, Heroic Resolve, Chariot, scenario rules) give nothing; failing = fled, nothing. It is already a per-model flag in matchInput.

REVIEW:
B1 66% direction. RECOMMEND Break Point = 66% of starting models (vanilla Break Point is a count; higher = tougher; fits the elite Uruk-hai). Alternative: the company breaks when reduced to 66% (much weaker: nonsense for an elite company). 
B2 All is Lost timing: RECOMMEND literal: only in the turn the company becomes Broken (before Priority). Alternative: any later turn start. 
B3 'Nothing further' for the fleeing company: RECOMMEND only Influence-for-participating (no Win/Draw Influence, no scenario rewards, no AtO Influence); injuries and experience still resolve (consequences, not rewards). Alternative: nothing but participation influence (no injury rolls/XP).
B4 Creatures count in startingModels: RECOMMEND yes. Alternative: no (they are not roster models).
B5 Composite model (Warg Marauder: 3 riders + a mount on one card): RECOMMEND count the 3 riders as the models (roster counts 3) and the casualty rule 'injuredWhen allRidersRemoved' for injuries; each rider removed is a casualty for the Break Point. Alternative: one model per card. Ask the user.
B6 Escaped/exited models (scenario edge-escape): RECOMMEND not casualties.
B7 Fled models for the 'fled' matchInput outcome vs casualties: both count for the Break Point; only 'casualty' rolls injuries.
B8 Temporary Wanderer: RECOMMEND counts in the starting models and as a casualty if removed.
B9 Percent not integer-friendly: integer test avoids floats (casualties*100 > percent*N).

WHAT THE APP MUST DO:
- Live match: per company show startingModels (computed from the match roster + creatures + temporary Wanderer, minus excluded), casualties (casualty + fled), the Break Point (percent x N / 100, display one decimal) and 'Broken' when the integer test holds at a turn start. On the turn boundary where it flips: banner 'Broken: every model tests before activating' and the All is Lost choice (before Priority), once. Per model tools: 'Courage test rolled: passed' sets brokenCourageTestPassed; 'failed' = fled (casualty count +1, no injury roll). Auto-pass sources (Stand Fast/Heroic Resolve) must not set the flag. Show scenarioExceptions for the scenario. Persist across restarts (live state).
- Aftermath: fledBroken -> influence = participation only, opponent counted as winner with full rewards; brokenCourageTestPassed -> +1 XP once; 'enemyBroken' Victory Point objectives read the opponent's Broken state (at the END of the game) so default that field from the live tracker.
- Recruit/Armoury: none. Company page: show the company's Break Point (50% / 66%) (breakPointPercentage already exposed).
DOMAIN SPEC (2026-10-21): docs/live-match.md 'Company break point in play'. Beads 36y.12-36y.17, question 36y.18 (Warg Marauder). Design: turn button is the only evaluation point; REVIEW defaults listed in the doc.
USER DECISION mqn.114 overrides B3 / the 'participation only' reading in defaultNotConfirmed: in All is Lost the fled company keeps its Against the Odds xp and influence bonuses (participation plus those, no Win/Draw, no scenario rewards); already built. Curator: please correct campaign.breakPoint.allIsLost text/defaultNotConfirmed accordingly.
Data complete (spec implemented in BC json, schema, validator, docs); closed by curator 2026-10-22.

title: Unbuilt rules 2: Against the Odds extras (Tool Kit, Temporary Wanderer, Ambush) in the BC json
description: Formalise Tool Kit, Temporary Wanderer and Ambush!: campaign.againstTheOdds (selectedAt, eligible, budget, per-bonus grants), matchInput fields, schema, validator, docs.
notes:
SPEC (curator, 2026-10-21). Data: campaign.againstTheOdds (selectedAt, eligible, budget; per bonus appliesIn, purchase, grants, expires), matchInput.perCompany toolKits / temporaryWanderer / ambushScenario. Schema + validator + docs done. The existing Reroll / Influence / Experience bonuses and campaign.aftermathEffects for them are unchanged (extended only with appliesIn); Healer's Kit items feed bead 36y.1.

SOURCES: AtO table "Tool Kit 30: You may only have one of each Kit, but their items may be distributed to any members and ignore all capacity / alignment rules" (Healer 5 Cram+2 Herbs; Explorer Scroll of Hidden Paths, 3 Mountain Boots, 3 Woodland Belts, Map; Scholar Ring of Warding, Badge of Courage, Lucky Talisman, Seeing Stone; Hunter 5 Envenom Weapons, Trophy Pelt, Concealing Cloak; Raider 5 Torching Brands, 5 Climbing Ropes, Dwarven Brew). "Wanderer 45: You may temporarily recruit a Wanderer for the match." "Ambush! 60: You choose the scenario." Intro: lower rated company selects 'after the roll on the Scenario Table was made, but before setting up'; bonuses add their Rating; 'must not exceed that of their opponent's'. Changelog 1.1: Wanderers a flat 45 in the AtO table; rating difference checked before AtO.

COMMON RULES (data): selectedAt afterScenarioRollBeforeSetup; eligible {company lowerRating, strictlyLower}; budget {ratingAfterBonusesNotAboveOpponent, inclusive true}. 'How much higher must the opponent be': the source gives no threshold beyond the budget, so a bonus is available only if opponent rating - own rating >= sum of chosen ratings (Ambush! alone needs a gap of 60; Wanderer 45; Tool Kit 30 per Kit). Equal ratings: no bonuses.

TOOL KIT: bonus toolKit, purchase {chooses oneKit, distinctKits true, maxPurchases 5}, grants {kind loanedEquipment, assignTo anyModelOfTheMatch, assignAt beforeSetup, ignores [capacity, alignment], stillApplies [heroOnly], addsRating false, expires endOfMatchAftermath, carriesOver false, usableByTemporaryWanderer false}. Items per kit: bonus.kits[].items (validated against equipment).
- When: chosen at selection time; items are assigned to models before setup (Brew is used at game start, scrolls at game start, Torching Brands in play); consumables used in the match are spent; Healer's Kit items act in the aftermath (bead .1).
- Capacity: a model may carry more Large/Small items than normal and Envenom Weapon (Evil only) may go to a Good model; Envenom Weapon (X) still needs a chosen weapon per item.
REVIEW T1: is one 30-Rating purchase ONE Kit (RECOMMEND; 'only one of each Kit' then means no repeats) or ALL five kits (too strong) or a kit per Rating only once? T2: after the match, are unused kit items kept? RECOMMEND no (loaned for the match incl. aftermath injuries, consistent with 'temporarily' and Reroll expiry). Alternative: keep unused ones as ordinary equipment (then also need rating/slot rules). T3: Hero-only items in kits (Herbs, Lucky Talisman, Map, Scroll of Hidden Paths, Seeing Stone): RECOMMEND still Hero-only. T4: can Warriors/temporary Wanderer carry? RECOMMEND any roster model of the match (Warriors and Heroes), not the temporary Wanderer. T5: model rating: kit items add NO Rating (the 30 pays for them).

TEMPORARY WANDERER: bonus wanderer, temporary true, grants {kind temporaryModel, from data.wanderers.items, count 1, ratingCost = bonus rating (45, replaces the Wanderer's own 60), influenceCost 0, goldCost 0, takesRosterSlot false, countsTowardsMaxModels false, countsTowardsBreakPoint true, exclusiveWithPermanentWanderer true, rollsInjuries false, gainsExperience false, persistsAfterMatch false, expires endOfMatch}. Wanderer rules (data.wanderers.rules): Hero in all ways, no Experience/Advancements, no Stand Fast, no Heroic Actions on the company, cannot buy gear.
REVIEW W1: with a permanent Wanderer already (max one at a time)? RECOMMEND not allowed. W2: counts against the 15-model cap? RECOMMEND no (never on the roster), but it counts in the starting models for the Break Point (it is on the board). W3: injury roll after the match? RECOMMEND none (it leaves). W4: which Wanderer: any of the 4 (no alignment data; wanderers.rules.alignment is not confirmed). W5: does its 45 replace its 60 in the company's Top Dog/Underdog comparison? No: comparison is before bonuses.

AMBUSH!: bonus ambush, grants {kind chooseScenario, from scenarios, replaces scenarioTableRoll, chosenBy lowerRatedCompany, rolesBy scenarioRules, duration thisMatch}. Interaction: the roll is made first, the bonus then overrides it. Scenarios with roles keep their own rule (25+ rating difference, checked before AtO, lets the lower company choose Attacker/Defender; otherwise dice). Nothing in the source makes the ambusher Attacker.
REVIEW A1: free choice of any of the 18 scenarios (RECOMMEND) vs only the listed tables. A2: roles: RECOMMEND scenario rules decide (offer both companies' roles as input). A3: if both... only the lower company can take it, so no conflict. A4: Ambush! with Fog of War/Tame the Beast etc. needs nothing special; Tame the Beast monster budget uses combined rating including AtO? Source silent: RECOMMEND combined rating after AtO bonuses is NOT used (changelog: rating difference before AtO; budget table by 'participating Battle Companies' rating) -> ask the user.

REPEATABILITY: the source never says whether Influence/Experience/Reroll/Wanderer/Ambush may be taken twice; today matchInput.againstTheOdds is a set (once each); Tool Kit alone has the 'one of each Kit' rule. Flagged in defaultNotConfirmed.

WHAT THE APP MUST DO:
- Before the match (pre-match / scenario step): show eligibility (lower company only, equal = none), a bonus picker with a running budget (sum of ratings <= gap) and the three new choices: Kit(s) with item-to-model assignment (any roster model), Wanderer pick, Ambush scenario pick (overrides the rolled scenario).
- Live match: show the loaned items on the model cards and the temporary Wanderer as a normal Hero card (no Stand Fast, no XP), included in starting models for the Break Point; consumables can be marked used.
- Aftermath: Healer's Kit items feed bead .1; the temporary Wanderer gets no injury roll, XP or progression and is dropped; unused kit items are dropped; Reroll as today.
- Recruit/Armoury: none (temporary things never enter the roster or armoury).
DOMAIN SPEC (2026-10-21): docs/matches.md 'Against the Odds before the game', docs/live-match.md 'Against the Odds items in a live match', docs/aftermath.md 'Against the Odds in the aftermath'. Beads 36y.6-36y.11. Question 36y.19 (Tame the Beast, no one waits).

Schema + validator + docs/definitions.md done.

SOURCES (BC doc, Equipment):
- Healing Herbs (Hero Only), Small (5), 2 Influence: "A Hero may elect to use their Healing Herbs at the end of any game they participated in that they were not removed as a casualty (ignoring Fleeing the Battlefield). If they do this, remove the Healing Herbs from their Equipment. All members of the Battle Company may add +1 to any Injury rolls that they must make at the end of the game. This is not cumulative."
- Wondrous Cram, Small (3), 2 Influence: "...may elect to use it at the end of any game they participated in that they were removed as a casualty (ignoring Fleeing the Battlefield)... remove the Wondrous Cram from their Equipment; additionally, do not roll on the Injury chart for them, instead they will automatically count as having rolled the Full Recovery result."

INTERPRETATION (data shape, exact):
healingHerbs = {kind injuryRollModifier, who allCompanyModels, activatedBy{carrier hero, requires [participated, notCasualty], fledModelIs notCasualty}, when beforeInjuryRolls, choice player, modifier +1, applies eachInjuryRoll, stackable false, usesPerAftermath 1, consumes oneItem, clamp [2,12], includesHeroReroll true}.
wondrousCram = {kind injuryRollReplacement, who carrier, activatedBy{carrier anyModel, requires [participated, casualty], fledModelIs notCasualty}, when beforeInjuryRolls, choice player, noRoll true, result fullRecovery, includesHealOneInjury true, consumes thisItem}.
- Who/when: elected by the player in aftermath step 1 BEFORE any injury roll. Herbs: one Hero carrier that took part and is not a casualty. Cram: the casualty model itself.
- Scope: Herbs +1 to the 2d6 TOTAL of every Injury roll the company makes this aftermath (Warriors and Heroes). Cram: that model only; it skips the roll, so Herbs/AtO rerolls are moot for it.
- Consumed: yes, both are removed from the Equipment when used; unused items stay. Not cumulative: two Herbs (Healer's Kit has 2) never give +2, so only ONE is consumed (usesPerAftermath 1).
- Who may take: Herbs Hero only (equipment restrictions [hero]); Cram any model of any company/alignment. Price: Herbs 2 Influence, rating 5; Cram 2 Influence, rating 3 (gold = rating). Small slot (one Small per model, Backpack to 4).

REVIEW (ambiguities; recommendation first):
R1 "(ignoring Fleeing the Battlefield)" is ambiguous. A) a model that fled the board is NOT a casualty for these rules; B) it refers to All is Lost (the company fleeing changes nothing). RECOMMEND A+B together: a fled model counts as not a casualty (Herbs carrier that fled may still use them, Cram has nothing to cancel since fled models roll no injury), and a company that fled voluntarily still resolves its items. Alternative: a fled model cannot use Herbs. Data flag activatedBy.fledModelIs.
R2 Modified total above 12 (12 + 1). RECOMMEND clamp to 12 (chart end; 12 gives Lesson Learned / Wounds of a Hero). Alternatives: no effect beyond 12 as a distinct result (same thing), or 13 reads as nothing (bad). A modified 12 counts as a real 12 (no 'natural' requirement; the injury chart has none).
R3 Does +1 apply to the Hero's T'is Just a Scratch re-roll? RECOMMEND yes (it is an Injury roll made at the end of the game). Flag includesHeroReroll.
R4 Cram result for a Hero: 'Full Recovery' is the 7-10 row, which also heals one Arm Wound/Leg Wound/Broken Honour. RECOMMEND include the heal (literal: the named result). Alternative: plain play-next-game only (flag includesHealOneInjury false). Cram never gives Valar/Wounds of a Hero extras and prevents Dead and retirement.
R5 Healer's Kit (Tool Kit) puts Herbs/Cram on 'any members' and ignores 'capacity/alignment': Hero-only is neither, RECOMMEND Herbs from the kit still go to Heroes only. Can the temporary Wanderer carry kit items? RECOMMEND no (Wanderers cannot have Equipment).
R6 Herbs used by a Hero that took part but a model that was Injured/not in the match cannot be the carrier: 'participated' = in the match roster.

WHAT THE APP MUST DO:
- Aftermath (step 1 Injuries): before showing the rolls, offer 'Use Healing Herbs' (if the company has a participating, non-casualty Hero carrying Herbs; one per aftermath) and per casualty 'Use Wondrous Cram' (if it carries one). Record in the sheet (perModel usesItem). Herbs: add 1 to each injury roll total (clamp 12), including re-rolls, and show it. Cram: no roll, set result = key fullRecovery of the chart (Hero: apply heal-one-injury choice). Remove the used item from the model's equipment (and free its slot) when the aftermath is committed, not before.
- Live match: nothing (items are used after the game). May show a reminder on the roster card ('Healing Herbs: use after the game').
- Recruit: none. Armoury: items sell as today (restriction hero for Herbs); list effect text from the effect. Wondrous Cram is not Hero only.
- Test: a Hero casualty with Cram never rolls Dead; two Herbs consume only one.
DOMAIN SPEC (2026-10-21): docs/aftermath.md 'Healing Herbs, Wondrous Cram and the Against the Odds items'. Beads: 36y.4 core, 36y.5 UI, 36y.11 Healer's Kit/AtO. All readings are curator recommendations, REVIEW: in docs.
Data complete (spec implemented in BC json, schema, validator, docs); closed by curator 2026-10-22.

title: Web: SSE endpoint /campaigns/{id}/matches/{match}/events, middleware Unwrap, graceful shutdown, wiring
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" > Live sync (SSE), "Changes needed in the existing server". Files: internal/web (handler, middleware.go), cmd/server (main.go, backend.go).
- statusRecorder.Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter so http.NewResponseController(w).Flush() works through the logger.
- Handler (protected GET): Subscribe; 404 not member/unknown, 409/204-less: match not open -> send `event: ended` and close; 429 at the caps (client polls). Headers Content-Type text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache no-transform, X-Accel-Buffering no. First write `retry: 3000` + comment, flush. Loop: Next -> for each company `event: company-<id>`, then `event: match`, `id: <seq>`, `data: {"seq":N}`; `event: ended` and return when Ended; `: ping` every 25 s; stop at ctx.Done and after 2 h. Every write sets SetWriteDeadline(now+10s) and flushes.
- cmd/server: start LiveHub, RegisterOnShutdown(hub.Close), keep ReadHeaderTimeout only (no WriteTimeout), no compression on the route.
- web declares liveMatches (spec) and a mock; handler tests with httptest + a fake core.LiveStream.
Acceptance / test cases
- headers and the first bytes appear before any event (client gets the response immediately); a batch with companies [3,4] yields events company-3, company-4, match with the same id; ended closes the response.
- non member 404, closed match gets `ended`, cap refusal 429; ctx cancel ends the handler without goroutine leak.
- the stream goes through the logger/recovery middleware chain and still flushes (test with the full Handler()).
- manual: run `make run` behind nginx/Caddy sample config note: events arrive within 1 s; kill -TERM ends the process within the 10 s shutdown without error log.
Depends on pib.14 (hub). Blocks pib.21.
notes: USER CLARIFICATION 2026-10-21: (a) Live matches must keep their state across server shutdown/restart: no live match information may be lost. All state lives in Postgres (log as truth, no in-memory state cache); the SSE hub only carries notifications, so after a restart clients reconnect and refetch. Add an acceptance test: write live actions, build a new service/hub on the same database (simulated restart), and check the folded state and log are identical, and that a reconnecting client resyncs. (b) The full log of a match is saved with the match permanently and can be reviewed at any time after it ends (no pruning, also after the campaign is finished), read-only, on the match page, with paging.
close_reason: SSE handler, Unwrap, tests; shutdown wiring was already in main (RegisterOnShutdown(hub.Close)). Note: live POST routes must not use s.once (identical +1 clicks would be swallowed).

title: Live db: open-match lock load, busy-company guard in Create/Update, ended NOTIFY
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" (Company lock and creation guards, Persistence). Files: internal/postgres/company.go (load), match.go, tests.
- CompanyState.OpenMatch (*OpenMatchRef, declared with pib.12 backend): on Read/Update load of a company, fill it with the open match the company is in (match_side_companies join matches WHERE NOT ended), like pendingRefs for Aftermaths; ignored on write. Add the field to CompanyState if the backend bead has not (coordinate through bead notes).
- matchRepository.Create: inside the transaction that already holds the campaign row lock, refuse with *core.CompanyBusyError{Company name, OpenMatchRef} when a company of any side is in another open match of the campaign (companies are per campaign, so the campaign scope is enough).
- matchRepository.Update: when Ended turns false (reopen) the same check (excluding this match), and when Ended changes either way `pg_notify('live_match', {"m":match,"c":0,"s":0,"k":"ended"})` in the transaction.
Acceptance / integration tests
- Read of a company in an open match has OpenMatch set; after End match it is nil; a company in an ended match is nil.
- Two concurrent Creates with the same company: exactly one succeeds, the other gets CompanyBusyError (errors.Is ErrRefused, errors.As gives the match number).
- Reopen of match 1 while the company is in open match 2 -> CompanyBusyError; reopen otherwise works as today.
- End and reopen each send one NOTIFY with k "ended".
Blocks pib.12 (backend).
notes: Added CompanyState.OpenMatch (internal/core/companystate.go, one field, uncommitted there: file shared). Existing tests creating a second match with the same companies adapted (raw SQL ends the first). Reopen locks the campaign row before the check.

title: Live core 2/3: LiveService (Init, Live, Apply, Undo, Log, AftermathDefaults) over liveRepository
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" (Transactions and locking, Aftermath prefill). Contract: internal/core/live.go (liveRepository, mocks via make generate). Files: live_service.go, live_service_test.go (mock liveRepository, companyRepository).
Implement core.LiveService with NewLiveService(live liveRepository, deps companyDeps-like (campaigns, companies, rules)). Methods as the web `liveMatches` interface in docs/live-match.md (except Subscribe, bead 3/3).
- Init(ctx, campaignID, matchID): per company of the match, from CompanyDetail (CompanyUnit.Stats for Wounds/Might/Will/Fate, Kind cavalry or mount equipment -> HasMount, Role hero or Kind monster -> CountsAsKill; Injured/AtHealers -> Absent) then liveRepository.Init (idempotent). Called by Matches.CreateMatch via a function field (like AftermathStarted) and lazily by Live/Apply/Log when Snapshot.Initialised is false.
- Live: ErrNotFound when the company is in no open match; Access from LiveAccessFor and the campaign status.
- Apply: access on the acting company (ErrRefused "Only the owner of <company> can change it", "The match has ended", finished campaign); unit must belong to companyID; inside liveRepository.Update fn: fold, Check, build LiveEntry (Text, Touches), return LiveChange{Append}.
- Undo: permission (owner of acting company or of a Touches company, organiser, admin); fn removes the entry, ValidateLog, returns LiveChange{Undo}; ErrLiveDepends passes through; ErrNotFound for an entry already undone.
- Log: sets CanUndo for the user.
- AftermathDefaults(ctx, id, matchID, companyID) ([]ModelSheet, bool, error): Field -> survived, Retreated -> fled, Casualty -> casualty; Gains from the flags/counts plus participated 1; absent units skipped; false when not initialised.
Acceptance / test cases
- Apply by non-owner -> ErrRefused and repository.Update not called with a change; admin and organiser pass; ended match / finished campaign refused for everybody.
- cross-company wound: owner of A wounds a unit of B -> entry has Touches [B]; B's owner can Undo it; a third player cannot.
- Undo that the fold rejects -> ErrLiveDepends and nothing stored.
- lazy Init: Live on a match without live data initialises once and returns the state; Init failure at CreateMatch does not fail the match.
- AftermathDefaults maps zones and gains as above; a match without live data returns false.
Depends on bead 1/3 (fold). Blocks pib.13, 3/3, and the frontend beads.
notes: Done (168a491). NewLiveService(live, campaigns, companies, matches, rules); WithHub(hub). Live/Apply/Undo/Log/AftermathDefaults/Init/Subscribe. Lazy init in Live/Apply/Undo/Log (not for ended matches). No generated mock for liveRepository: tests use an in-memory fakeLive with the Postgres semantics (live_service_test.go). Eager Init at CreateMatch is wired in pib.12.

title: Live core 3/3: LiveHub, Subscribe, caps, graceful close
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" (Live sync, Hub). Contract: LiveEvent, LiveBatch, LiveStream, liveFeed in internal/core/live.go. Files: live_hub.go, live_hub_test.go (fake liveFeed, no database).
- core.LiveHub: NewLiveHub(feed liveFeed, matchCompanies func(ctx, matchID) ([]int64, error)); Start(ctx) runs feed.Run(ctx, publish, resync); Close() ends every stream (cmd/server wires httpSrv.RegisterOnShutdown(hub.Close)).
- LiveService.Subscribe(ctx, user, campaignID, matchID) (LiveStream, error): ErrNotFound for non members / unknown match, ErrRefused when the match is not open or at the caps (10 per user, 50 per match; Close releases).
- A stream is a mutex-guarded pending LiveBatch + a wake chan of capacity 1; Next(ctx) blocks and returns the merged batch (Companies deduped, Seq max, Match true, Ended); resync marks all the match's companies and Match; an `ended` event sets Ended. First Next after Subscribe returns an immediate batch with all companies at the current seq (initial sync, also what Last-Event-ID resumption means).
Acceptance / test cases
- 1000 events published to a stream nobody reads leave one pending batch (no goroutine or memory growth; run with -race).
- two streams of two matches: an event reaches only its match; Close of one stream does not affect the other and frees its cap slot.
- 11th stream of one user and 51st of one match are refused; a closed stream frees the slot (also when ctx is cancelled).
- resync delivers all companies; hub.Close makes Next return an error for every stream.
- Next returns on ctx cancel without leaking the goroutine.
Depends on pib.28 (service) and pib.10 (real liveFeed; tests use a fake). Blocks the web SSE bead.
notes:
REVIEW: no per-event authorisation re-check (spec asked for one); auth at connect, events hold ids only, fetches are authorised. REVIEW: stream max age 2h instead of idle 2h (no idle: pings).
USER CLARIFICATION 2026-10-21: (a) Live matches must keep their state across server shutdown/restart: no live match information may be lost. All state lives in Postgres (log as truth, no in-memory state cache); the SSE hub only carries notifications, so after a restart clients reconnect and refetch. Add an acceptance test: write live actions, build a new service/hub on the same database (simulated restart), and check the folded state and log are identical, and that a reconnecting client resyncs. (b) The full log of a match is saved with the match permanently and can be reviewed at any time after it ends (no pruning, also after the campaign is finished), read-only, on the match page, with paging.
Done (168a491). NewLiveHub(feed) (no matchCompanies callback: each stream keeps the companies of its match, given by LiveService.Subscribe), Start(ctx), Close(). Streams freed by Close or request ctx cancel (context.AfterFunc). Initial batch = all companies at current seq. Restart acceptance: core (TestLiveSurvivesARestart, fake store) and Postgres (internal/postgres/live_restart_test.go, real NOTIFY): same log, same folded state, reconnecting client resyncs, post-restart write reaches stream. Web SSE bead pib.30 can use core.LiveService.Subscribe.

title: Live rules: company lock (CompanyState.OpenMatch) and creation guards
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" (Company lock and creation guards). Spec: docs/live-match.md Match start rules 1-3. Types OpenMatchRef, CompanyBusyError, LockMessageOpenMatch are declared in internal/core/live.go.
Implement (internal/core only; the Postgres side is bead pib.29)
- CompanyState.OpenMatch *OpenMatchRef (clone in Clone, doc: filled by the repository, ignored on write); Locked() checks it first with LockMessageOpenMatch, then Aftermaths. CompanyDetail.OpenMatch for the page.
- Audit every roster action for the Locked() call; add it where missing (level-up roll/choose/reroll/path, promote, carry, hire/dismiss wanderer, anything that spends gold or influence). RenameUnit, SaveFormation, SaveCemeteryOrder and organiser grants (GrantReward) must stay allowed: test it.
- Matches.CreateMatch: ErrRefused "Finish the aftermath of Match N first." for a company with a pending aftermath through a field PendingAftermaths func(ctx, campaignID, companyID) ([]AftermathRef, error) (wired in cmd/server to AftermathService.PendingAftermaths) - default per question pib.24; the busy-company refusal comes from the repository (pib.29) as *CompanyBusyError and must pass through unwrapped enough for errors.As.
- Matches.CreateMatch calls LiveService.Init through a function field (bead 2/3) and ignores its failure (lazy Init covers).
Acceptance / test cases (mock repositories)
- every action in the audit list returns ErrRefused "Match 3 is running; finish it first." when OpenMatch is set, and works when nil; both set: the open match message wins.
- CreateMatch with a company that has a pending aftermath is refused naming the match; a CompanyBusyError from the repository is returned as is.
- RenameUnit / SaveFormation / GrantReward succeed with OpenMatch set.
Depends on pib.24 (default a) and pib.29 (db); blocks pib.22 and pib.16.
notes: Done. Locked(): OpenMatch first (message wins over an aftermath), then Aftermaths. Audited every companies.Update: added Locked to Carry, RecruitSpecial and LevelService.mutate (roll, choose, reroll, path); RenameUnit, SaveFormation, SaveCemeteryOrder, grants and aftermath/bury stay allowed (test). Matches.CompanyAftermaths (named so, not PendingAftermaths: the field would clash with the AftermathService method in the cmd/server facade) refuses a company with a pending aftermath (pib.24 default: no); *CompanyBusyError from the repository passes through; Matches.LiveInit called after Create, failure ignored. Wired in cmd/server/backend.go; hub started in main, closed by RegisterOnShutdown. The facade embeds liveSvc (compile-time check of the method set in cmd/server/live_wiring_test.go). pib.24 answered by default; the user may flip it.

title: Live core 1/3: pure fold of the log, action validation, texts
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" (State is a fold of the log); contract: internal/core/live.go; rules: docs/live-match.md.
Files (new, internal/core): live_fold.go, live_fold_test.go. Pure code, no repository.

Implement
- FoldLive(inits []LiveUnitInit, entries []LiveEntry) LiveState (units by company -> []LiveUnit; Gains map). Entries are the not-undone ones in Seq order.
- (LiveState) Check(a LiveAction, byCompany int64) (resolved LiveAction, touches []int64, text string, err error): validates against folded state and returns the action
  with Set resolved to Delta, the other companies touched, and the log text. Errors: ErrInvalidLive (joined, fit to show: Count/Caused 1-9, SavedByFate 0..min(Caused,Fate), Note <= 200, unknown Stat/Why/Part, Delta 0, Targets empty, a target equal to the attacker),
  ErrRefused with a reason (unit not in the Field, target not in the Field, Fate 0, tracker out of 0..Start, absent unit, no mount, mount already in that state).
- Refold-check for undo: ValidateLog(inits, entries) error returns ErrLiveDepends (naming the first entry that fails) when any entry is not valid against the state before it.
- LiveAccessFor and CanUndoEntry(user, entry, companiesOfEntry owners, organiserID) are here too (declared / to add).
Semantics (all from the spec): wounds 0 -> Zone casualty, reason "Wounded by <unit> (<company>)" or "Wounds lowered to 0"; zone priority retreat > died/Wounds 0 > field;
woundedEnemy flag when Caused >= 1 (even if all saved); fatePrevented flag on the target and on the actor of a `fate`; slainHeroOrMonster +1 only when the target CountsAsKill and its rider part reaches 0;
a Mount part drops MountWounds (at 0: Mounted=false) and never makes the rider a casualty; broken sets brokenCourageTestPassed once; return clears retreat/died and lifts Wounds 0 to 1.
Acceptance / test cases (table tests)
- every kind: stat +/-, set (resolved to delta), wound (rider, mount, saved by Fate, kill Hero, kill Warrior gives nothing, kill Monster), fate (and refused at 0), broken, retreat both reasons, died, mount off/on, return from each zone.
- xp flags: woundedEnemy once for two declarations; slainHeroOrMonster counts 2 for two Heroes; all-saved wound still gives woundedEnemy.
- zone priority (retreated unit with Wounds 0 is Retreated); retreated/casualty units cannot act or be targeted; absent units cannot.
- undo validity: removing a Fate +1 that a later Fate spend needed -> ErrLiveDepends; removing a wound declaration with later independent entries is fine and restores Wounds/Fate/flags/zone; removing a retreat with a later return -> ErrLiveDepends.
- fold is deterministic for the same input and does not mutate it.
LABELS stay backend. Blocks pib.13 (needs FoldLive) and the LiveService bead.
notes:
REVIEW: 'Return to the battle' is its own action kind 'return' instead of an undo (avoids the ambiguity of which entry took the unit out; the spec's 'not unique' case). REVIEW: aftermath badge is on the whole unsaved default, not per value.
Done. FoldLive/LiveState.Check/ValidateLog/CanUndoEntry in live_fold.go. LiveState.UnitName/CompanyName funcs (set by the service) put names in texts and in the casualty reason ('Wounded by X (Company)'); LiveState.Unit/Company return units with zone+reason. REVIEW: stat changes are allowed on a Field unit and on a wounds-casualty (+ brings it back), refused for retreated/died units. A wound declaration fully applies each target in order inside Check (sim) so later targets see earlier results.

title: Live db: match_live tables, liveRepository, liveFeed (LISTEN/NOTIFY)
description:
Design: docs/architecture.md "Live match" (Persistence shape, Transactions and locking, Live sync). Contract: internal/core/live.go (liveRepository, liveFeed, LiveSnapshot, LiveChange). Can start now: the interfaces are declared.
Migration 00014 (check the next free number): match_live, match_live_unit, match_live_log with the constraints and indexes of the design. Store accessors Store.Live() (liveRepository) and Store.LiveFeed() (liveFeed; the Store must keep the connection URL). Payload is versioned jsonb {"v":1,...} of the LiveAction (json tags are the adapter's).
- Init: INSERT match_live and the units in one tx, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; ErrNotFound when match is not in the campaign or a company is not in the match.
- Read: snapshot without lock (Initialised = match_live row exists; Entries not undone, ascending seq; Ended from matches).
- Update: SELECT matches FOR NO KEY UPDATE (does not bump revision), re-read snapshot, call fn, then Append (seq = match_live.seq+1, UPDATE match_live) or Undo (set undone_at/by/seq, bump seq); `SELECT pg_notify('live_match', payload)` for the acting company and each Touches company, payload {"m","c","s","k":"changed"}; all inside the tx; the error of fn is returned as is and rolls back.
- Log: not undone, newest first, before/limit, joins users for By.
- LiveFeed.Run: dedicated pgx.Connect (not the pool), LISTEN live_match, WaitForNotification with 30 s timeout then ping, reconnect with backoff 1 s..30 s, onResync after each (re)connect, returns on ctx done; parses payload k "changed"/"ended".
Acceptance / integration tests (make test-integration)
- Init twice stores once; Read before Init is Initialised=false; deleting the match cascades.
- 20 concurrent Updates on one match get seq 1..20 without gaps or duplicates (unique (match_id, seq) never violated); an Update after the match is ended sees Ended=true in the snapshot.
- Update that returns an error stores nothing and sends no NOTIFY; a committed Append notifies exactly once per touched company (listener test: a second connection LISTENs).
- Undo marks the entry out of Log/Entries and takes a seq; the entry stays in the table (audit).
- LiveFeed: delivers events after commit only, calls onResync on start and after the listening connection is killed (pg_terminate_backend) and continues.
- CHECK constraints reject negative starts; composite FK rejects a unit of a company not in the match.
Labels db. Depends on nothing; blocks 3/3, pib.12 db part is a separate bead.
notes:
Schema questions answered in docs/architecture.md Live match > Persistence shape: seq counter in match_live (locked via matches row FOR NO KEY UPDATE), no FK on unit_id, undone_seq column, payload versioned jsonb. Migration number: next free. Please reply in a note if the live Update lock on matches conflicts with matchRepository.Update.
USER CLARIFICATION 2026-10-21: (a) Live matches must keep their state across server shutdown/restart: no live match information may be lost. All state lives in Postgres (log as truth, no in-memory state cache); the SSE hub only carries notifications, so after a restart clients reconnect and refetch. Add an acceptance test: write live actions, build a new service/hub on the same database (simulated restart), and check the folded state and log are identical, and that a reconnecting client resyncs. (b) The full log of a match is saved with the match permanently and can be reviewed at any time after it ends (no pruning, also after the campaign is finished), read-only, on the match page, with paging.
DB answer: live Update locks matches FOR NO KEY UPDATE; matchRepository.Update uses FOR UPDATE, so they conflict and serialise (intended), no deadlock: reopen takes match lock then campaign lock, Create takes campaign lock only. REVIEW: match_live_log.match_id references match_live (not matches) so a log row needs Init first; Update on an uninitialised match returns a plain error after fn (service must Init first). REVIEW: an undo of an unknown or already undone entry id returns ErrNotFound; undo bumps match_live.seq, so entry seqs have gaps after undos (unique per match still holds). title: Armoury: armour upgrades (Armour, Heavy armour, Dwarf armour; 1 influence per stage) are not offered for any unit in any company
description: FOUND in the Shire audit, affects all 37 companies. BC rules (Armoury > Wargear): 'Upgrade Armour by one stage: None & Light -> Armour -> Heavy Armour & Dwarf Armour, 1 influence per upgrade, rating (1/5) per upgrade'. The json has data.wargear.armourUpgrade (stages, influencePerUpgrade 1, rating, gold) but no Go code reads it (grep armourUpgrade in internal: none): no armoury row, no purchase, and vanilla profile options such as Ranger of the North 'Armour' (5 pts) / Hobbit options show as option-unbuyable (Shire audit: 'Ranger of the North / Armour'). Warriors may buy armour only if the profile has an Armour option (stage must match the option); heroes may take any armour upgrade ('including Armour upgrades available to any profile in the charts'). Needs: offer per unit from its current armour stage (profile wargear + equipment), price 1 influence / gold 1/5, applies Defence change (statChanges), Beast units may upgrade armour (amy.17), Barding is separate. Needs a design pass (armour item per stage, replaces previous stage, dropped = discarded not downgraded per optional rule). Proposed owner: backend-planner then coder.
notes: User decision 2026-10-21 (4): implement armour upgrades; buying replaces current armour with next tier (unarmoured -> armour -> heavy); heroes may only buy tiers units in the company already have.

title: Any campaign creator can squat a rules edition name+version and fill the shared rules store
description: Repro: as you@example.com create a campaign with 'My own file' vanilla whose name is the shipped edition and version 9.9 (hash = sha256 of compact JSON). Then /admin/rulesets upload of a different file with the same name+version is refused: 'A different file with this name and version is already stored. Delete the stored one first if no campaign uses it.' but the campaign uses it, so the admin cannot fix it without removing the campaign. Also each creator upload (up to 16 MB, any number) lands in the admin list. Severity: gap. Question for the user: should uploads by non-superusers be scoped (not part of the shared list/name uniqueness), rate/size limited, or kept as is?
notes: OPTIONS: (A) keep as is (any creator may add files; name+version is global). (B) Scope uploads: a file uploaded while creating a campaign is private to that campaign (not in /admin list, not subject to the global name+version uniqueness), only superusers' uploads join the shared list. (C) Keep sharing but only superusers may reserve a name+version of an edition shipped with the app, and add a per-user quota (count/size) on uploads. RECOMMENDATION: B for the squatting (the admin's upload then never conflicts) plus a small per-user cap (say 5 files, 16 MB each) so the store cannot be filled; needs your decision because B changes the rules-file model (docs/auth.md, admin.md, the picker).

title: Company schema: migration + companyRepository (Read, Update, Create)
description: Database master: answer as notes (1) jsonb for progress and pending ok? (2) deferrable unique position or gapped integers? (3) fallen snapshot as jsonb? Needs core.CompanyState from the contract bead.
acceptance_criteria: Tables companies, company_units, unit_equipment, fallen_units per docs/architecture.md; Update locks the company row and rolls back when fn errors (test: two concurrent Updates serialise); unit positions unique per company and replaced wholesale; Create returns ErrHasCompany on a duplicate (campaign, owner); integration test round-trips a full CompanyState.
notes:
Persistence questions for database-master: see acceptance; planner proposal in docs/architecture.md 'Persistence shape'.
DB MASTER ANSWERS. (1) jsonb for progress, injuries and the pending processes: yes. They are opaque to SQL, versioned with the rules code, never filtered on. Give every jsonb blob a top-level "v" integer so the Go side can migrate old shapes lazily; add CHECK (jsonb_typeof(col) = 'object'). Anything queried or constrained (owner, position, level, injured, sent_to_healers, resources) stays a column. (2) Positions: dense 0-based integers with UNIQUE (company_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, and the repository rewrites the whole roster on Update (delete + insert of company_units rows in one tx is NOT wanted since unit ids must be stable: UPDATE by id, INSERT new, DELETE removed, all inside the tx; deferred constraint makes swaps legal). No gapped integers: a reorder is a wholesale replace and gaps buy nothing. CHECK (position >= 0). Same for fallen_units, but fallen order is only ever appended/reordered via SaveCemeteryOrder, same scheme. (3) fallen snapshot as jsonb: yes, a frozen copy (profile, wargear, path, level, XP); the fallen never change and must survive rules changes. Plus columns company_id, position, fell_in, fate, fell_at. REVIEW: unit ids never reused: IDENTITY ALWAYS, a unit keeps its id when it moves to fallen_units (fallen row stores original unit_id in a UNIQUE column, no FK). REVIEW: Update = SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the companies row, load state, run fn, write back, commit; fn error rolls back. Repository type is returned by Store.Companies() like Store.Rulesets(), because interface method names collide across repositories. Blocked on 7v5.18 (core.CompanyState) so no migration yet.
DONE. Migrations 00006 (campaigns, needed first for the FK) and 00007 (companies, company_units, unit_equipment, fallen_units); Store.Companies() in internal/postgres/company.go. REVIEW: pack is text[] and saved orders are bigint[] columns (not jsonb); Order/Graveyard ids are not FK-checked (stale ids ignored). REVIEW: unit_equipment origins gear/bought/dropped, no for_weapon (not in UnitState). REVIEW: Create refuses units with preset ids; owner must be a campaign member (FK -> ErrNotFound). REVIEW: new units added in Update get ids in the DB but the caller's state is not refreshed; re-Read to learn them. Unit moving roster->cemetery keeps its id.

COMPANY RULES, HERO UPGRADES AND COMPANY PAGE DATA (done: tools/bc/company_effects.py (new), companies.py fix, build script, schema, validator, docs/definitions.md; validator 0 errors).
A. HERO UPGRADES. Rulebook: Path Progression (S l.624) 'Regardless of availability, a Hero may swap ANY result for their Company Specific Hero Upgrade if they don't already have it'; Company page glossary (S l.1989) 'Any Hero may choose to replace a result from their Path with a Company Hero Upgrade'. So: ANY result (not only the minor-special-rule one), once per hero (only if it does not have it), regardless of path or of whether the result is available. It replaces the chosen RESULT; the other pair stays (player picks among: result A, result B, upgrade). The user's belief (only the minor-rule result) is not what the rulebook says. Data: companies[].heroUpgrades[{name, flavour?, restriction?, specialRule}]; the rule text is data.keywords[name=specialRule].definition (all 44 upgrades have text; fixed Moria 'Callous Leadership' whose text was split between flavour and definition). flavour missing for 5 (Fiefdoms x4, 'She Hungers for Sweeter Meats' : none in the rulebook). restriction (a subgroup): Fiefdoms Dol Amroth/Lossarnach/Lamedon/Blackroot Vale, Wanderers in the Wild 'Hobbit' (second upgrade), Cirith Ungol 'Spiders', Wolves of Isengard Orc (Savage Charge) / Warg (Feral Charge). Companies with 2 upgrades: Shire (Of a Party Sort, Throwing Stones), WitW (You Have My Sword + Hobbit one). Also each upgrade is now an effect {kind:heroUpgrade, name, specialRule, restriction?} in companies[].effects[].
Upgrades by company: Minas Tirith The Charge of Gondor; Osgiliath Remember Today; Fiefdoms 4 (see above); Fornost Defiance; Arnor Foresight of the Seer; Last Alliance There Were Some Who Resisted; Rohan Back on your Horses!; Helm's Deep One Final Blow; Druadan Know All Paths; Erebor Lordly Quality; Defenders Defender; Lothlorien Blessing of the Golden Wood; Rivendell Veteran of the Old Wars; Thranduil Bladelord; Durin's Folk The Stubbornness of Dwarves; Iron Hills Stubborn Brilliance!; Lake-Town Moneybags; WitW You Have My Sword + I Have My Own Sword (Hobbit); Shire Of a Party Sort, Throwing Stones; Mordor Orcish Brawler; Cirith Ungol Animosity + She Hungers... title: Re-roll and aftermath bonus sources (Against the Odds etc.)
description: see notes
notes:
GOLD (done). Source: sources/battle_companies_rules.txt l.214-215 (Company Creation 'Gold'), l.2062 (60-point rule), l.203 (Custom Selection).
(1) When: the rule sits in company creation ('Starting Battle Company'); nothing says Gold is ever gained or spent later, nor whether unspent Gold carries over (UNDECIDED). (2) Price: 'treat the initial Rating (Point Value) of the Equipment, Creature or Wanderer as its Gold value, ignore the Influence cost'. Data: equipment rating {warrior,hero} (data.equipment.items[].rating); creatures/wanderers = points (5/10/5; Wanderers 60 = unaffordable with max 6 Gold). Wargear Gold price is NOT stated (inferred = its Rating (1/5 etc.)). NEW property data.*.items[].gold = that price ({warrior,hero} or a number) on equipment, wargear (+armourUpgrade, companies[].uniqueWargear), creatures, wanderers. (3) Wargear with Gold: 'additional Wargear for starting models as long as Warriors are still legal to one of their profile's Options'. Heroes: no limit stated (Heroes may take any wargear in the Influence armoury rule, l.1388-1392); inferred that Hero in the Making rules apply as for Influence. (4) Slots/limits/rarity: not restated for Gold; only the Custom Selection sentence says 'must still adhere to any restrictions'. Recommended: all still apply. (5) Gold cannot buy units or Influence (nothing says it can). (6) 60 rule: starting company Rating + Gold ~ 60 before Might/Will/Fate (a custom-company guideline: l.2062; campaign.company.startingPoints=60).
NEW campaign.gold = {startingGoldPath, ignoresInfluenceCost, when, spendableOn[{kind,price,priceIs,path,condition}], cannotBuy, stillApplies, startingTotal{target,counts,excludes,source}, carryOver:null, inferred[], undecided[]}.
QUESTIONS: G1 Does leftover Gold carry over into the campaign or is it lost after company creation? (recommend: lost/only at creation; show the counter as 'start only') G2 Gold price of a piece of wargear: its Rating (warrior 1/hero 5) as assumed, or its Influence cost? (recommend Rating, consistent with equipment) G3 Do Heroes in the Making pay the hero rating (5) for wargear with Gold? (recommend yes) G4 Do equipment slots and Wargear Limits apply to Gold purchases? (recommend yes) G5 Can a Hero take wargear outside its profile with Gold? (recommend yes like Influence) G6 Must the starting company total exactly 60 with Gold? (recommend: warn only).
AGAINST THE ODDS RE-ROLLS (done). Sources of re-rolls/bonuses that touch the aftermath (all in new campaign.aftermathEffects[]): (a) AtO Reroll bonus (campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[key=reroll]): chosen by the lower-rated company after the scenario roll, costs 15 rating, 2 re-rolls usable at any point of the game or for the War's Aftermath, each re-rolls a single die or a single result; NEW fields count:2, usableIn:[game,warsAftermath], affects, expires/carriesOver:false (inferred: 'for the match'). (b) AtO Influence (+2 win/+1) and Experience (+2 per model win/+1) bonuses: gains structured. (c) Scenario rewards: Chance Encounter 'Rendezvous' (victor gets +1/-1 on its first Reinforcement roll next aftermath: a modifier, not a re-roll), Scavenge the Battlefield (free Equipment up to 2 Influence if all 6 markers), Rescue 'Survival of the Fittest' (+1 XP to each surviving Leader), Baggage Train (+1 Influence if all Cargo): data.scenarioDetails[name] text + aftermathEffects[]. (d) Rules that re-roll inside the aftermath without a counter: Hero Injury 6 'T'is Just a Scratch' optional re-roll (campaign.injuries.hero[justAScratch].reroll), progression unavailable results (progression.hero.resolution.unavailable). (e) Game-only re-rolls (NOT aftermath, no counter): Lucky Talisman (Fate rolls), path/hero-upgrade rules (Reading the Portents, Usurper of Kings, etc.), banner. None of the company rules or hero upgrades grant aftermath re-rolls. Bonus Progression Rolls: the rulebook mentions scenarios may list free advancements, but no scenario in the data does.
QUESTIONS: R1 Do unused Against the Odds re-rolls carry over to the next match? title: Rule questions digest (open questions for the user)
description: Consolidated list
notes:
OPEN RULE QUESTIONS DIGEST (consolidated; ordered by impact; items the user already decided are excluded: arm wound gear bans, healable injuries per method, unlimited retries, Valar capped, creatures chip+card, wanderers dismissible with no refund + hero injuries, pony swap built, hero-in-the-making rolls pending, one-window hero level-up). Each: question / options / recommended / what changes.
A. LEVEL-UP
1. 'Taking the extra roll': when a hero rolls a 5 on its path (Courage or Intelligence +1 'and take your other roll too'), what if the other roll is not usable, or is also a 5? e.g. rolls 5 and 12 (12 already owned). Options: (a) re-roll the unusable one; (b) lose the extra. Recommend (a). Changes: hero.resolution.rollAgain handling in the roll loop.
2. 'Unusable result': a hero rolls two results and one cannot be used (Strength already at the limit). Re-roll only that result, or both? Recommend only that one. Changes: hero.resolution.unavailable.action.
3. Stat limits written '(+1)': is that +1 over the stats the unit had when it became a Hero, or over the base model profile? e.g. a Warrior with Strength 3 promoted to Hero; limit (+1) means 4 max. Recommend: over the profile at the moment it became a Hero (the rulebook tool note tracks Base + Increase). Changes: how `maxIncrease` is computed, need to store 'increase' per stat.
4. Same minor rule twice with different choice, e.g. Poisoned Attacks (Bow) and Poisoned Attacks (Spear). Recommend: allowed if the choice differs. Changes: duplicate check uses name+parameter.
5. May a Warrior who rolls 'Hero in the Making' choose the promotion instead only when a promotion exists? Recommend yes (else hero). Changes: option shown or hidden.
6. Rolls left when a Hero has learned everything on its path: wasted (recommend) or kept? Changes: pending-roll counter stops.
B. MAGIC (new)
7. Casting Value floor: can improvements take 3+ down to 1+/2+? Recommend never below 2+. Changes: castingRule.floor (already 2, flagged inferred).
8. Row 10 'improve Casting Value by 1' has no '2 improvements max' text (rows 3 and 7 do). Same cap everywhere? Recommend yes. Changes: cap check in app.
9. May a Sorcerer learn a power it already knows? Recommend no. Also Fury (X): choose species when learning. Changes: excludeKnown.
10. A Hero built from a profile that already casts (e.g. a Shaman) taking the Sorcerer path: use the profile's casting value for its own powers (recommend) and the list's for newly learned ones. Changes: per-power casting stored on the hero.
11. Tactician, Sharpshooter, Soldier add no Heroic Action at start (only the universal Move/Shoot/Combat). Confirm that is right and nothing else is given at start. Changes: startingHeroicAction stays null.
C. INJURIES / HEALING (assumptions still to confirm)
12. A Hero sent to the healers is 'Injured' next game (not in rating, misses the game): confirm. Same for Leg Wound: Move has no floor. Fearful from the 2nd Broken Honour disappears when healing brings it back to 1. The player chooses which injury is healed. Recommend: all four yes. Changes: derive Fearful/Move from counts; healers sets Injured.
D. GEAR AND CREATURES
13. Axe of Lossarnach / Dunlending War Axe / Easterling Halberd are 'spear or two-handed' (halberd: 'pike or two-handed'). Does the player pick the mode per fight (recommend) or at purchase? e.g. Shield bonus disappears only while used two-handed. Changes: needs a per-fight toggle or simplification (show both rules).
14. Baggage Pony: do items stored on it still count toward the Bow/Throwing limits, and if its owner dies, is the load lost? Recommend: stored items do not count; load is lost with the owner (rules say creatures and equipment are lost when the owner dies). Changes: limit calculation + death handling. Also: one swap per member per visit (recommend yes).
15. Do Creatures count towards the Bow/Throwing/Cavalry percentages (recommend no) and Wanderers (recommend yes, they are Heroes; a Marksman with a longbow counts)? Changes: limit calculation.
16. Goat in the wargear list uses the War goat profile (recommend yes, no other Goat exists). Wanderer: can it ever become Leader/Sergeant when those die (recommend no). Changes: mount profile pointer / succession rule.
