title: Level-up system as data: progression rolls for warriors and heroes
description: Curator-lite job; see notes
notes:
SOURCES: sources/battle_companies_rules.txt l.296-352 (Aftermath order), 474-520 (Progression), 520-640 (limits, paths), path tables l.640+. JSON: campaign.progression, campaign.characteristicLimits, campaign.experience, data.paths[], data.minorSpecialRules, data.companies[].advancements, campaign.rating.
RULES: a model (warrior or hero) that gains 5 XP rolls for Progression. XP is a running total, never spent (a promoted/Hero-in-the-Making model keeps it): rollsEarned = floor(XP/5), several can wait; scenario 'bonus progression rolls' are extra and do not count against XP. Timing: War's Aftermath step 3, after injuries and experience, before influence. No Influence or Might adjustment is allowed for progression (only the Against the Odds Reroll bonus, which re-rolls 'the War's Aftermath for a single result').
WARRIOR (1d6, campaign.progression.warrior.table): 1-2 noChange; 3-5 promoted = take a promotion from data.companies[].advancements[] (match from.unit + from.wargear; several matches: player picks; exchange all characteristics, keep wargear the new profile allows; keeps XP); if no promotion exists: Courage and Intelligence +1 each to max 3+ (warrior.noPromotion); 6 heroInTheMaking: becomes a Hero, +1 Might/Will/Fate, keeps XP, picks a Path, rolls as Hero from next game; may instead take the promotion. New: progression.warrior.effectsByKey.{noChange,promoted{promotion,fallbackWhenNoAdvancement},heroInTheMaking{becomesHero,grants,selectsPath,retainsExperience,advancesAsHeroFrom,alternative}}.
HERO (campaign.progression.hero + data.paths[]): choose Path when becoming Hero; each level-up roll 2d6 TWICE (two sums), pick one result, only on own Path. Row shape: paths[].progression[{roll 2..12,text,options[]}]; options[] are ALTERNATIVES (player picks one). option types: specialRule{specialRule}, improveStat{stats[],amount,mode:oneOf|(all),maximum,rollAgain}, minorSpecialRule{maxTotal}, heroicAction{maxTotal} (NEW: was text only, now generated for every non-Sorcerer path, roll 10), magicalPower, improveCastingValue{amount,maxPerPower}, oneOf{options[]} (nested alternatives). rollAgain on roll 5 = also take the other pair's result. Unavailable result (stat at maximum, rule already owned, minor-rule/heroic-action total reached, spell duplicate): re-roll that result until one is available; if nothing is possible the hero 'has learned all'. A hero may swap any result for the Company Hero Upgrade (data.companies[].heroUpgrades) if not owned. New: progression.hero.resolution{dice,pairs,choose,onlyOwnPath,unavailable,companyHeroUpgrade,rollAgain,optionsAre,statLimits,ratingEffect}; progression.xp, .timing, .influenceAdjust=false, .mightAdjust=false, .rerollSource.
STAT LIMITS: data.paths[].maximums[stat] = {max | maxIncrease | best}; overall ceiling campaign.characteristicLimits.peak (Might/Will/Fate max 3; Will 6 for Tactician/Sorcerer = peak.willMaxOverrides); new characteristicLimits.lowerIsBetter [shoot,courage,intelligence] (improving = lower number) and limitKinds explains max / maxIncrease (above the profile the unit started with) / best (lowest value allowed). Rating: an increase only adds rating when it takes the stat beyond characteristicLimits.average (campaign.rating.hero.perPoint 5/10); text says 'equal or under average do not add'.
WANDERERS: no XP, no advancement. CREATURES: On Their Own Path, none. Death of a Hero: the Warrior with most XP is treated as rolled Hero in the Making (campaign.injuries.deathOfAHero).
ALGORITHM (hero): rolls=floor(xp/5)+bonus-taken; loop: roll 2d6 twice -> rows; keep only rows whose options are applicable (some option applicable: improveStat with at least one stat below its max/limit; specialRule not owned; minor rule/heroic action count < maxTotal; magicalPower/castingValue available); a row not applicable is re-rolled; offer to the player the applicable rows (+Company Hero Upgrade swap); player picks one row then one option (and stat/choice inside); apply: increase stat by amount (clamped at maximum; if maximum:6 for Will etc), add rule/action/spell; if rollAgain also apply the other roll's result; recompute rating (above average only). Warrior: roll d6 -> effectsByKey.
QUESTIONS (recommended answer): 1) Does the stat limit for 'maxIncrease' count from the profile at promotion or the base unit profile? (from the profile the Hero was created with, i.e. at Hero in the Making incl. Might/Will/Fate 1; track base+increase as the rulebook's tool note does). 2) Roll 5 'take your other roll too': if the other roll is also a roll 5, or unavailable? (apply normally; if unavailable re-roll). 3) May the player choose the other pair if both are available and the first is rollAgain? (yes, but then no extra roll). 4) Re-roll of unavailable results: re-roll both dice pairs or just that pair? (just that pair). 5) Can a Hero use a Reroll (Against the Odds) on progression? (yes, single result). 6) Several rolls waiting: resolve one by one, in any order, choices after each (yes). 7) Hero in the Making via roll 6 happening in the same aftermath as pending rolls: does XP-earned rolls beyond 5 then use the hero chart? (yes: remaining rolls are hero rolls; 'from next game on' hold: recommend the first hero roll in the NEXT aftermath, ask user). 8) 'Alternatively forgo the Hero's Journey and take the Promotion': allowed only if a promotion exists (recommend yes). 9) Promotion keeps current XP and remaining rolls (yes). 10) Casting value / magical power duplicates and Combat Synergy (X)/Poisoned Attacks (X) parameter choices: store the parameter per rule; may the same minor rule be taken twice with different X? (recommend yes if X differs). 11) Do level-ups of units with Company special profiles (Wild Warg -> rider) count as Promotion? (yes, via advancements). 12) May a hero that has exhausted its path still gain XP for later rolls (yes, rolls are wasted).
NOTE: open questions of this bead are consolidated in the OPEN RULE QUESTIONS DIGEST (see the 'Rule questions digest' bead); answered ones: see user decisions in that bead.
ANSWERED by the user: hero level-up is one window with both rolls; if only one result can be taken the player must take it, re-roll only when BOTH are unavailable; Hero in the Making rolls as hero the next time it earns 5 XP and keeps pending rolls; (+1) maximums count LEVEL-UP increases only (not gear/base/promotions), backend tracks increases per stat; Courage/Intelligence total cap 3+ also applies to gear in battle. JSON: progression.hero.resolution.window/unavailable, warrior.effectsByKey.heroInTheMaking.firstHeroRoll, characteristicLimits.increases. DEFAULT not confirmed (recommended answers): roll-5 'other roll' unusable -> re-roll it; same minor rule twice only with a different parameter; forgo hero for promotion only if a promotion exists; rolls after the path is exhausted are wasted; Reroll bonus may be used on a progression result. Closing.

title: Rules brief: healing injuries (warriors and heroes) for the unit Heal button
description:
RULES QUESTION from the app implementer. Answer by APPENDING to this bead's notes (bd update <id> --append-notes ...); do not edit app code. Cite the rule source (sources/ page or definitions/ path + field) for each point.

1. Which ways exist to heal an injury for a WARRIOR and which for a HERO? For each: cost, requirements (roll, influence, phase, building/scenario), effect.
2. When is healing allowed (between games only? any time?) and is a roll involved (dice, target numbers, modifiers)?
3. How are injuries represented in definitions/ (structured data or text only)? Which fields/IDs should the app read? Name any missing data the curator must add.
4. Failure outcomes (death, permanent injury, lost influence) and whether the player may adjust a roll with influence as in recruiting.
5. How the app should model it: inputs the UI must collect, state to persist per unit, and edge cases (injured units excluded from rating, multiple injuries).
notes:
RULES BRIEF (advisor). Source S = sources/battle_companies_rules.txt (Battle Companies rulebook), D = definitions/battle_companies/battle_companies.json.

1. WAYS TO HEAL
Only one explicit rule: "Treat Injuries", the third use of Influence in Step 3 Company Management (S l.1380-1384; D campaign.influence.spend[key=treatInjuries], text only; D campaign.injuries.healing.{warrior,hero}, text only).
 WARRIOR: pay 1 Influence, the Injured condition is removed (no roll). Effect: unit may play the next game and counts again for rating.
 HERO, two options, each costs 1 Influence:
  a) Attempt: roll D6, success on 5+, removes one Injury from the Hero. Roll may be raised with extra Influence "the same way as a Might point" (see Q4).
  b) Send to the healers: automatic (no roll), but the Hero misses the next game; one Injury is removed.
 Indirect/free heals (not purchases, happen in War's Aftermath injury step, S l.298-352; D campaign.injuries):
  - Hero injury roll 7-10 "Full Recovery": may heal one Arm Wound, Leg Wound or Broken Honour (effects incl. "healOneInjury"); roll 11 and 12 are Full Recovery without the heal-one clause.
  - Wondrous Cram (equipment, hero or warrior; D data.equipment.items[name="Wondrous Cram"], S l.1693): spend it when removed as casualty -> no injury roll, counts as Full Recovery (prevention, not healing of an existing injury).
  - Healing Herbs (hero only, D data.equipment.items[name="Healing Herbs"], S l.1618; Healer's Kit = 5 Cram + 2 Herbs): +1 to all the company's injury rolls that game, not cumulative. Not a heal button feature.
 Warrior Injured also ends on its own after the one missed game (S l.346); a Heal on a warrior only skips that missed game.

2. WHEN / ROLLS
Healing is a Step 3 action (post-battle sequence: 1 Injuries, 2 Experience, 3 Progression, 4 Influence; then Step 3 spend; then Step 4 ratings; S l.296-302, 1349-1404). So between games only, after the injury rolls of that game are resolved, and only with Influence available (Influence is gained in step 4 of Aftermath: 2 per scenario +1 draw +2 win; D campaign.influence.gains). No building/scenario requirement exists. No stated limit on how many treatments per unit or per aftermath (AMBIGUOUS: nothing says "once per injury"); each costs 1 Influence minimum. Dice: warrior none; hero D6 target 5+; no other modifiers in the text.
Ambiguity: the rulebook does not say a Hero's treatment must come after a game in which the injury occurred; "between games" is the only sensible reading.

3. DATA IN definitions/
 Structured: D campaign.injuries = {roll:"2d6", warrior:[...], hero:[...], deathOfAHero, healing}. Each entry {roll:[lo,hi], key, name, effects[], text, optional retireAtCount, grantsAtCount, stat, influence, experience, optionalReroll}.
  Warrior keys: dead (2-3, effects remove), injured (4-5, missNextGame), fullRecovery (6-11), lessonLearned (12, experience "D3").
  Hero keys: dead (2), armWound (3, retireAtCount 2, effects noShield/noTwoHandedWeapon/noPike/noBow), legWound (4, retireAtCount 2, stat.movement -1), brokenHonour (5, retireAtCount 3, grantsAtCount {"2": specialRule "Fearful"}, effects noStandFast/noHeroicActionsOnCompany), justAScratch (6, missNextGame, optionalReroll), fullRecovery (7-10, effects fullRecovery+healOneInjury), protectionByTheValar (11, stat.fate +1), woundsOfAHero (12, influence "D6").
 The healing rule itself is TEXT ONLY: campaign.influence.spend[key=treatInjuries] (no cost/target/roll fields) and campaign.injuries.healing.warrior / .hero (strings). Both mention the 5+ and 1 Influence only in prose.
 App should read: campaign.injuries.hero[key in armWound|legWound|brokenHonour] for the persistent (healable) injuries and their stat/effect/retire/grant data; key "injured" (warrior) and effect "missNextGame" (warrior injured, hero justAScratch) for the missed-game state.
 MISSING, curator should add (e.g. to campaign.injuries.healing, structured): warrior {cost:1}; hero {cost:1, roll:"d6", target:5, modifiable:true, perExtraInfluence:1 (+1 each, see Q4), maxExtraInfluence: null/unspecified}; hero healers {cost:1, auto:true, missNextGame:true}; list of healable injury keys (armWound, legWound, brokenHonour); and campaign.influence.spend[treatInjuries] cost:1. Also a flag marking which hero keys are "permanent injuries" (currently inferred from retireAtCount). Nothing says which hero results other than those three count as an "Injury" to remove; "T'is Just a Scratch" is a missed game (like Injured), not a persistent injury - the reading used here.

4. FAILURE / MODIFYING THE ROLL
 Hero 5+ attempt: the source gives no failure penalty. A failed attempt just costs the 1 Influence spent and leaves the injury (no death, no new injury, no extra loss stated; Influence is not refunded - paid per attempt: AMBIGUOUS whether the cost is paid per attempt or only on success, the wording "spend 1 Influence to ... attempt" implies per attempt). The player may retry by paying again (not forbidden; AMBIGUOUS, no per-aftermath cap stated).
 Influence modifier: "same way as a Might point": each extra Influence adds +1 to the D6 (Might raises a die by 1 per point, never lowers, never above 6; mesbg_rules.md l.2349). So 4 needs +1, 3 needs +2, 2 needs +3, 1 needs +4; a natural roll of 6 needs nothing. 5+ already succeeds on 5 or 6, so the roll is raised after seeing the dice. Unlike recruiting, no max of 3 Influence is stated for treating (recruiting cap: D campaign.influence.spend[adjustRoll] maxPerRoll 3, text S l.1379, and recruiting can go up or down; treating can only go up). Cannot exceed 6 so at most 4 extra Influence are meaningful. Is a natural-6 check "natural 6 can't fail"? Not stated; with +1 per point there is no fail on 5-6 anyway.
 The healers option and the warrior option have no roll, so no adjustment.
 Hero "Dead"/forced retirement is only an injury-roll outcome (Q1), not a healing failure.

5. APP MODELLING
 Inputs for a Heal action on a unit (UI): unit; for a Hero, which injury to remove (choose among its current Arm Wound / Leg Wound / Broken Honour) and method (attempt vs healers); for attempt: the D6 result (manual entry or the app's dice) and the number of extra Influence points to spend (0..4); company Influence balance check (total cost = 1 + extra, or 1 for healers/warrior). Warrior: just confirm, no inputs.
 State per unit to persist: injured flag (misses next game; already core.Unit.Injured at internal/core/company.go:318); for Heroes a list/counts of persistent injuries {armWound, legWound, brokenHonour} (count, not boolean, because retireAtCount 2/2/3 and Broken Honour 2 grants Fearful); the stat effects they cause must be reversible (Move -1 for each leg wound; Fearful granted at 2nd Broken Honour should be removed when the count falls back below 2: AMBIGUOUS, the rule says healing "resets the count", so derive the effects from the counts). Company Influence balance (decrement; ideally a log entry). A "missesNextGame" flag distinct from healing (the healers' Hero is also Injured/out of rating for the next game, consistent with S l.1403).
 Edge cases:
  - Injured units are excluded from rating (S l.1404; D campaign.rating.text). Healing a warrior or a Hero's Injured/healer state: removing Injured puts its points back. A Hero sent to healers becomes Injured (miss next game, not counted in rating) while the injury is removed immediately.
  - A Hero can hold several injuries (e.g. one Arm Wound, one Leg Wound, Broken Honour x2); each treatment removes ONE injury (player's choice; the rule does not say who chooses: assume player). Full Recovery roll heals one more at injury time, also player's choice.
  - Warrior: only valid when Injured. Hero attempt: only valid when it has at least one healable injury; healers: same. "Injured" for a hero (justAScratch miss-next-game) is not removable by the 5+ attempt per the text ("an Injury"): AMBIGUOUS; recommend allowing the 1-Influence removal of Injured for heroes only if the curator confirms.
  - Dead heroes/warriors are removed entirely, no heal. Creatures roll no injuries (S l.1717; D data.creatures).
  - Injured clears automatically after the missed game (next game recorded) even without paying.
  - Healing happens after the injury rolls and before Step 4 rating; the rating shown should update.
CURATOR-LITE UPDATE: structured data added (tools/bc/core.py -> regenerated json, schema, validator, docs/definitions.md; validate: 0 errors).

Hand-and-a-half weapons are class two_handed so they are disabled too: confirm. (2) Which injuries are healable: assumed only armWound/legWound/brokenHonour; is Injured/Just a Scratch (miss next game) removable from heroes by the 5+ attempt? (3) Failed attempt: Influence lost, retry allowed same aftermath? maxPoints null (unbounded, ceiling 6). Is a roll of 5-6 plus extra Influence moot (yes)? (5) Leg Wound minimum Move: none stated. (6) Who chooses which injury is healed: assumed player. (7) Does the healers' missed game also make the Hero Injured (excluded from rating)? assumed yes. title: Gear annotations in the Battle Companies JSON: classes and granted rules (curator)
description:
GEAR ANNOTATIONS IN THE BATTLE COMPANIES JSON (task for the definitions-curator)

WHY. The unit cards of the app (My Company page) show every unit's equipment with an icon and colour per CLASS, sorted by
class, and add the special RULES an item grants to the unit. The vanilla file cannot tell: only 101 of its 233 gear items
have a `type`, each has at most one, and nothing links an item to the rule it gives. The app currently guesses
(core.ClassesOfGear in internal/core/company.go) and, for rules, grants a rule when an item shares its name with a
keyword. That guess must become data. Decision from the user: put it in the BATTLE COMPANIES JSON; do NOT add a fourth
JSON file. The vanilla file stays untouched.

WHERE / SHAPE (you decide the details and update the schema; keep the style of `data.wargear` and `data.equipment`):
  data.gearAnnotations = {
    "text": "what this section is",
    "items": [ { "name": "Long-bladed spear",
                 "classes": ["spear", "melee"],        // ordered; the first is the MAIN class (icon lead, sorting)
                 "grants": ["<rule name>", ...],       // special rules the item gives its bearer (optional)
                 "ranged": {"range": 24, "strength": 2},// only bows, crossbows, throwing weapons (optional)
                 "evidence": "short phrase of the item's text that justifies this",
                 "status": "derived" | "curated"         // derived = by the script, curated = you decided
             } ] }
  Items are keyed by name like everywhere (vanilla names: first occurrence wins; BC names win over vanilla).
  Class vocabulary (an enum in the schema; the app's core.EquipmentClass uses exactly these):
    mount, melee, two_handed, spear, shield, armour, bow, crossbow, throwing, banner, instrument, other
  An item can have several classes: a "blade-spear" ("this is a spear and a two-handed blade") is ["spear","two_handed"];
  a spear that is also a hand weapon adds "melee". Plain hand weapons, swords, axes, maces, daggers are "melee".
  Rule of thumb: classes say what the item IS (what you could point at), not what rules it has.

SCOPE. Every piece of gear that can appear on a unit card of a Battle Company:
  (a) every item named in the `wargear` of a vanilla unit that a Battle Company can field (through the company
      starting units, reinforcement tables, unitAliases, options, deltas), and every vanilla gear item those units can buy;
  (b) the items of `data.wargear.items`, `data.equipment.items`, the companies' unique wargear and anything the BC
      document lets a model carry; (c) mounts (Horse, Warg, Fell Warg, Goat...).
  Produce a coverage report: items by class, items classified `other` (each with a one-line reason), items with grants.

HOW. Add `tools/bc/gear.py` (or similar) that derives candidates from the item texts (patterns such as "This is a
spear", "two-handed", "Range, Strength", "mount", shield and armour modifiers in `modifiesStats`, the vanilla `type`)
and a small hand-written table of decisions that override it; the generator writes the section into the BC file. Never
hand-edit the generated JSON. Extend `tools/validate_definitions.py`: schema + class enum, every `grants` entry must resolve
to a vanilla keyword or a BC rule, every gear item reachable from a company has exactly one annotation, no duplicates.

GRANTS NEED CARE. A definition that merely MENTIONS a rule ("a model with a banner ... Shielded ...") does not grant it.
Only record a grant when the text or the BC document says the bearer gets the rule. Everything unclear goes to the user as
a list (item, text, your proposal), never guessed. Classes are mostly derivable; grants are curated.

RULES (as always): copyright (sources/ stays local), never silently drop or invent data, list every guess for the user's
confirmation, keep the pipeline reproducible, update docs/definitions.md and tools/README.md, commit only your own paths
and only when asked.

HAND-OFF. When done: write `tools/gear_review.md` (generated: one row per item with name, classes, grants, ranged, evidence,

title: Company backend: units, resources, limits and persisted unit order
description: Prototype on fakes (uncommitted when written): core.CompanyDetail {Influence, Gold, Limits, Roster}, CompanyUnit {Name (nameable), Type, Role leader|sergeant|hero|warrior, Kind infantry|cavalry|monster|monstrous_cavalry, Points, Equipment[{Name, Category bow|throwing|other, Bought}], SpecialRules}, core.CompanyLimits (bows, throwing weapons, cavalry: 33.33% of the company rounded up, heroes included, from definitions limits), core.OrderUnits(units, savedOrder). Default order: leader, sergeants, other heroes, regular units. The player's own order must be persisted per company (e.g. company_units.position, set by a reorder action) and applied by OrderUnits; new units fall in by default order. Real data comes from the loader (x8p): unit type, options, wargear, special rules resolved BC > vanilla. Unit kind and role derive from the rules data; Bought vs starting equipment needs a flag on the owned item. Other players' companies get the same detail read only.
notes:
Update after the card prototype: CompanyUnit now carries Stats []Attribute (from core.VanillaBook: the vanilla 'stats' list in order Mv FV SV S D A W C I | M W F, with Might/Will/Fate only for heroes that have some, plus the company's Boost per attribute), Equipment[{Name, Class mount|melee|two_handed|spear|shield|armour|bow|crossbow|throwing|banner|instrument|other, Bought, Stats, Description}] sorted by core.SortEquipment, Rules[{Name, Description, Source unit|path|equipment, Spell, Casting, Range, From}] sorted by core.SortRules, Level and XP (total earned; 5 per level-up roll, pending = (XP - Level*5)/5). The loader must provide what core.VanillaBook does now: unit profile by name, keyword/gear/power definitions, unit types (-> Kind via core.KindOf; monstrous cavalry = Cavalry + Monster). Gaps found: vanilla gear 'type' is missing for 132 of 233 items so core.ClassOfGear falls back to name heuristics (a curator-supplied class would be better); gear that grants a rule (spear support, spikes, crossbow, company instrument) is not linked in the data, the fake grants a rule when an item shares its name with a keyword; Battle Companies point costs and path rules come from the BC file (the fake takes vanilla points and path text by rule name). Role (leader/sergeant/hero) and the unit's level/XP/bought items are company state to persist. The level-up button needs a roll endpoint (several rolls in a row, level only gained when rolled); persist the unit order.
Recruit and armoury prototype (fake.Campaigns): the backend must provide, per company: maxModels (campaign.company.maxModels 15, elite 12, per-company override), reinforcements.influence (2-4 per roll), reinforcement chart rows and special chart (D6 ranges -> unit/nothing/specialChart, wargear, choice, blocksFurtherRolls), specialUnits [{unit, influence, rare, choice}] (Moria: Cave Troll 15), unique wargear. core.BCBook is the lookup the loader replaces. Actions: Recruit(roll 0 = random), RecruitSpecial, BuyEquipment, Armoury(unit) with a reason when not buyable (carried, hero/cavalry/evil/good restrictions, slots, bow/throwing limits, influence). Persist: influence and gold, recruits, bought items with the unit they belong to, unit slots derive from size (large 1, small 1, Backpack +3 small). Open rules questions for later: adjusting a reinforcement roll with influence (+/-1 each, max 3 across both charts), 'choice of options' recruits (player picks any profile option except banner/warhorn...), rare units the company cannot have (take a lower result), warriors may only buy wargear matching one of their profile's options and heroes any wargear of the company's charts, wargear limits when a roll would break them, creatures attached to leader/sergeants (do not take a roster place), equipment lost when its owner dies.
Now also prototyped on the fake (the backend must do the same): roll adjustment (-3..+3, 1 influence each, first chart only), pending 'choice of options' recruit (influence spent, unit joins when chosen; options = vanilla unit options minus banner/war horn/war drum; persists across requests, blocks other recruits), armoury visibility rules (only items the unit may take; lack of influence/slots shown; warriors: wargear matching their profile options, heroes: any wargear of units in the company's charts incl. their starting wargear). Item icons derive from the name (core.IconFor) with generic small/large fallbacks; the gear annotation bead could provide an explicit icon key.
Equipment can be dropped (DropEquipment(unit,item)): any item, also from the profile, no refund; it frees the slot and the company limit. A full limit (bows, throwing weapons) is a reason shown (Blocker 'limit'), not a rule that hides the item. Open: the BC rule says a warrior may drop wargear only if it translates to another option of its profile (rating difference marked down), heroes freely; the user wants any unit to be able to drop anything, so confirm the rating/points effect of dropping.
Dropping now follows the BC rules (core.DropReason): equipment always droppable; heroes drop wargear they chose/bought freely, profile wargear only with the optional rule 'heroes may discard any wargear' (campaign.company.text.youDontHaveMySword; a per-campaign setting to add, off by default); warriors may drop wargear only if what remains equals another option of their vanilla profile (or the plain profile), never profile wargear. Points follow: unit points = vanilla points + rating of what it chose or bought (BC wargear/equipment rating, warrior or hero column), so a drop marks the rating down. NOT done: the hero rating from stat improvements (5 per Might/Will/Fate/Move/Fight/Strength/Defence point, 10 per Attack/Wounds, 5 per special rule: campaign.rating.hero), the company rating's exclusion of injured models, and the drop of a hero's profile gear changing rating (BC: no change unless the group decides otherwise). Persist a unit's chosen option wargear, bought items, dropped profile items (the fake keeps them as dropped names).
Done on the fake and to be done by the backend: hero rating from stats (BCBook.HeroRating: base warrior points + 5/pt Might Will Fate Movement Fight Strength Defence, 10/pt Attack Wounds above the warrior profile AND the average BC profile, 5 per path special rule; wargear/equipment not in profile or options at the hero column when Attacks+Wounds >= 3, else warrior column; named/monster heroes: vanilla points + gear), injured units excluded from the company rating (CompanyUnit.Injured; Treat Injuries and the injury chart are not built), per-campaign optional rule 'heroes may discard any wargear' (CampaignSettings, chosen at creation, persisted with the campaign), recruit as steps: RollRecruit (pays the price) -> RecruitState -> ConfirmRecruit(adjust +-3 total across both charts; special chart gives a second free roll) with the in-progress state persisted. Still open: minor special rules rating (5 each, max 10), company limit overrides (limitOverrides, e.g. Osgiliath bows 50%), rare units a company cannot have, wargear limits breaking a roll (take the next result down or adjust), company notes beyond reinforcements.
Gear annotations are consumed now: core.BCBook.Annotation (classes with lance/missile/consumable, aliases, grants, grantedTo mount, ranged, weaponModifier), core.GearAnnotation, class-based limits with limitExemptions/limitOverrides (computeLimits, BCBook.Limits), named unit upgrades as badges (IsUnitUpgrade: class other and no slot), Barding as steed armour (isSteedArmour matches the name: ask the curator for a field if more items need it), the Armory tab (ArmouryEntries: every offer with per-unit reasons) and BuyEquipment from it. GearMatchesOption now matches an item that is several things by name only. The Envenom Weapon modifier is shown on the unit's first melee weapon: the real purchase must record which weapon it was bought for.
Formation: the backend owns the unit order. SaveFormation(company, ordered unit ids) persists it (e.g. company_units.position, replace the whole order in one transaction; reject ids that are not in the company); loading a company applies core.OrderUnits(units, savedOrder): saved order first, units not in it (recruits since) after, in the default order leader/sergeants/heroes/regular. The default order only applies until the player has saved once.
close_reason: Final pass: implemented by 7v5.17-.19 (company schema, BuildDetail, CompanyService.SaveFormation persists unit order in companies.order). Verified in code/tests (core companies_test, postgres services_test) and in the running app (roster, limits, recruit as eowyn at 1280).

title: Rulesets store (backend): content-addressed rules files
description:
Replace internal/fake.Rulesets with a Postgres-backed store implementing web.rulesets (Default, Lookup, Store).
- Table keyed by hash (hex SHA-256 of the file with insignificant whitespace removed = core.RulesetHash), kind (vanilla|battle_companies, later glossary), name, version, size, the compacted JSON, uploaded_by, created_at. Same file uploaded twice stores once.
- Store MUST recompute the hash from the upload and check kind with core.RulesetMeta; never trust the client's hash. Already built and tested in core: RulesetHash, RulesetMeta (name = game, version = appVersion for vanilla / version for BC until files carry uniform fields, see the metadata bead).
- Browser flow (done, static/js/ruleset_picker.js): hash in the browser, GET /rulesets/{hash}, upload only if unknown. Endpoint is login-protected; consider rate limiting and a size cap (16 MB now).
- Defaults: the app's own definitions/ files, embedded and registered at startup with Default=true (hash computed at load, not hard-coded).
- Validate uploads against the JSON schemas in definitions/*.schema.json (Go JSON-schema lib) before storing; reject with core.ErrInvalidRuleset.
- Garbage: files no campaign references and nobody pinned can be pruned later (admin section).
- Feeds the loader (x8p): campaigns with the same (vanilla, bc, glossary) hashes share one set of in-memory maps.
notes:
Decision: vanilla files are identified by name + version (game + appVersion; core.RulesetKind.IdentifiedByEdition), the hash is kept as an integrity check. Store/Find must return the stored vanilla file of the same edition even when the uploaded hash differs; Battle Companies files stay hash-identified. Open risk: a corrected re-release of the vanilla data under the same game + appVersion would be ignored; an admin 'replace this edition' action (admin section bead) or an appVersion bump is the way out. Log (do not show) when the hash differs for a known edition.
Update: a vanilla upload whose name+version are stored with a different hash is an ERROR (core.ErrEditionExists, GET /rulesets/{hash} answers 409), not silently mapped to the stored file; this protects against edited vanilla files. Battle Companies and glossary files are hash-identified; name/version are top-level fields now (RulesetMeta reads them; vanilla uses game/appVersion). core.KindGlossary exists. The UI shows 'name · version' plus an 8-char hash label for every file. The fake registers the real definitions/ files as defaults.
close_reason: Final pass: Postgres rulesetRepository + core.Rulesets (hash recomputed, kind check, JSON-schema validation via jsonschema/v6, ErrEditionExists, embedded defaults); tests pass in make test-integration. Pruning unused files is tracked by j62 (admin section).

title: Glossary restructure: one term per rulebook concept, synonyms-only aliases, richer see-links
description: Several terms merge distinct concepts (Cavalry Charge = Extra Attack + Knock to the Ground; Special Strikes; Spears and Pikes; Brutal Power Attacks = Rend/Hurl/Barge; Close Combat Weapons; Dismounting). Split them so one rulebook heading = one term, aliases only for real synonyms, and give every term see-links (e.g. phases link to what happens in them). Phases currently hold the rulebook one-line overview only; add the chapter intros. Needs a full review pass of all terms.
notes:
Scope decision: glossary entries are BRIEF reminders, not rule chapters (players know the game). Keep the rulebook's overview/first paragraphs, trim long sections (Priority, Heroic Actions, War Beasts, Courage Tests...), do not copy the detailed phase chapters.

Progress (uncommitted): glossary_terms.py restructured to 108 terms (split Special Strikes, Spears/Pikes/Lances, Close Combat Weapons, Cavalry Charge, Dismounting, Brutal Power Attacks, Heroic shouts, durations, Bows/Crossbows, Armour); first=N trimming; phase chapter intros; see-links on every term; build_glossary fixes (drop caps, running heads, split paragraphs). validate: 0 errors. Guesses awaiting confirmation: alias 'hand weapon' on Close Combat Weapons; aliases Steed(s), Remount, 'Duration: X'.
Round 2: Special Strikes family removed (only in the local rulebook PDF, whose copyright says 2022; absent from vanilla/BC) - confirm which edition the PDF is. 'first' kept only as extraction boundary; 36 long chapters are synth=True with summaries in tools/glossary_summaries.json. Added Special Weapons, Master-forged Weapons, Staff of Power, Changing the Weapons on a Model, Slingshot, Elven Cloaks, The One Ring. 'hand weapon' alias removed (vanilla equipment name).
Round 3: the first PDF was the 2022 manual (Special Strikes etc. are gone in 2024). Rebuilt from the 2024 manual (/Users/iuya/Downloads/ilide.info-mesbg-rules-manual-2024-pr_*.pdf, converted with pdf2md using the P22MackinacPro-Bold heading face): 201 terms, 57 summarized (tools/glossary_summaries.json, written against the 2024 text). New 2024 concepts: Activation Phase, Intelligence Tests, Unit Types, Chariots, Trample/Stampede, Heroic Tiers, etc. Dropped: Special Strikes family, Special Weapons, Changing the Weapons on a Model, Remounting, Cavalry Steeds. Old 2022 text kept locally as sources/mesbg_rules_old.md.
Round 4: pdfPage renamed rulebookPage (printed page = PDF index - 1, checked against 'see page N' cross references); added Siege Engines and Sieges chapters (234 terms, 64 summarized); army-building chapters deliberately left out (BC builds companies differently). Open: alias review with the user; Heroic Tiers follower counts are army-building text, decide whether to keep.
Round 5: tier terms (Heroic Tiers, Hero of Legend/Valour/Fortitude, Minor Hero, Independent Hero) and the manual's Last Stand removed (BC: all Heroes are Minor Heroes, BC has its own Last Stand; Heroic Challenge's tier condition is therefore always met - note for the BC data). Bow and Throwing Weapons are categories (variants are not aliases; added Throwing Spear term). Dwarf armour = Heavy Armour (+2; per user and BC table), Heavy Dwarf Armour (+3) separate. Pennant alias removed.
Round 6 (alias review): kept as synonyms Broken Force, Close Combat Weapons, Elven-made, Slingshot, Engaged, Duel, To Hit, To Wound, Commander, Crew. Split into own terms: Characteristics (+ Move/Fight/Shoot Value, Strength, Defence, Attacks, Wounds, Courage, Intelligence), Break Point, Supporting (Spear keeps the weapon), Strike, Impact Hits, To Wound Chart, Knocked to the Ground, Magical Powers, Casting Value. 'Duration: X' aliases removed. 246 terms. Still to decide: Turn, Swim, Active/Passive, Objective, modifier, within, D6/D3/2D6, Stairs, Scatter, Shooting Attack(s), Casualty, Combat, Knocked Flying aliases.
Round 7: Turn split from Turn Sequence; Swim Test, Objectives, Scatter, Casualty, Knocked Flying added as terms; Fortress Stairs folded into Stairs (alias); aliases removed: modifier, Objective(on Markers), Scatter, Shooting Attack(s) (moved to How to Shoot), Casualty, Knocked Flying. Kept: Active/Passive, within, D6/D3/2D6, Combat. 252 terms.

title: Definitions loader: first occurrence wins for duplicate names
description: The loader that merges the vanilla + BC jsons into queryable maps must resolve a name defined more than once in vanilla by taking the FIRST occurrence (verified against the official rules for Enchanting Song, Mercenary Ambush, Relentless Advance, The Honour of Lamedon; same for units Galadhrim Knight / Guard of the Galadhrim Court pending confirmation). BC json can pin a different winner when the rule of thumb fails. Once the loader exists, the 4 copied keyword overrides (+2 units) in the BC json can be dropped (see tools/bc/core.py DUPLICATE_DECISIONS).
notes:
Design (see docs/definitions.md): in-memory immutable maps; ruleset id = SHA-256 of the compacted JSON of its vanilla/BC/glossary documents; cache keyed by that triple, built once (singleflight) and shared by all campaigns with the same hashes; uploaded documents stored once per hash (content-addressed) in the DB, campaigns reference the hashes; concept graph precomputed at load.

title: DECISION: Ranger of the North replacement when the chosen role slot is already held
description: The rule says the Ranger 'may immediately take the role of Leader or Sergeant' but the company already has a Leader and two Sergeants. title: Curator: separate 'situational' from 'cancelled by own gear' on gear stat bonuses
description: R8 (v4v): the app adds a stat bonus to the unit only when it is unconditional. In gearAnnotations, abilities[defenceBonus].conditional is true for Shield/Iron Shield/Pavise because their bonus can be cancelled by the unit's own gear (bow, two-handed, pike) - the app decides that from the unit's items and keeps the bonus by default - while the Pavise's real condition (not while Engaged) is read from notWhileEngaged and Small Shield from against. Please add one explicit flag for bonuses that hold only in a game situation the app cannot see (e.g. situational:true / 'situation' text) on defenceBonus abilities and on statChanges, and keep conditional for self-cancelling. statChanges[].conditional true is already treated as note-only.
notes: 2026-10-22 curator: already in the data since 23efc12/1d9ce2c. conditional=true now means situational only (Pavise, Small Shield, Elven Glaive; validator enforces it, docs/definitions.md describes it); Shield/Iron Shield conditional=false, loadout cancellation (cancelledByClasses/Items, liftedByRules, cancelledByTwoHandedUse) stays computed. title: Review/rules: BC keyword overrides replace the vanilla text of units that carry the rule natively (Keen Sight on Crebain shows the Falcon text)
description:
Companies: Burning of the Westfold, Hill Tribes of Dunland (Crebain: Keen Sight); Angmar & Carn Dum (Werewolf: Feral Charge); Westfold, Muster of Isengard, Gundabad (Feral Uruk-hai, Uruk-hai Berserker, Gundabad Berserker: Oblivious to Pain); Harad (Abrakhan Merchant Guard: Burly).
Evidence: data.keywords 'Keen Sight' (source Falcon, overrides Keen Sight) says 'Enemy models within 12" of a Falcon that is separate from its Hero may not benefit from Stalk Unseen' while vanilla Keen Sight (what the Crebain profile lists) says 'Enemy models within 12" of this model gain no benefit from Stalk Unseen'. Resolution order is 'BC wins' (ruleTip/RuleSet), so the chip on the Crebain card, the audit tooltip and the glossary link show the Falcon rule. Feral Charge and Oblivious to Pain only differ by wording ('this Hero' for 'a Werewolf' / 'this model'); Burly is identical.
Options: (A) curator: a BC keyword that is the narrower, context-bound variant of a vanilla rule (Keen Sight for the Falcon creature) must not carry overrides, or gets its own name (Keen Sight (Falcon)); hero-generalisations (Oblivious to Pain, Feral Charge) stay. (B) Go: special rules a unit lists on its own vanilla profile resolve to the vanilla definition first; BC overrides apply to rules granted by a path, upgrade, creature or company. 
Recommendation: A for Keen Sight (clear defect, data only), accept the Hero wording of the others; B only if more such cases appear. Not touched by the auditor (curator owns definitions/).
close_reason: Option A done: a creature's rule that shares a vanilla name is a creature-bound variant and gets its own name 'Keen Sight (Falcon)' without overrides (build_battle_companies.py), so the Crebain's vanilla Keen Sight keeps the vanilla text. Hero generalisations (Oblivious to Pain, Feral Charge) keep overrides (wording-only differences). App check: anything matching the Falcon rule by the name 'Keen Sight' must use 'Keen Sight (Falcon)' (nothing in tools/internal does).

title: Review: Helm's Deep Elf limit (33%) is worked out on the maximum company size (15 -> 4) and rounds down, bows and cavalry use the current size and round up
description: BC Helm's Deep: 'No more than 33% of your company may include models with the Elf keyword.' The app (companybuild.go keyword limits; recruitBlock) allows int(33% x 15) = 4 Elf models whatever the company's size and counts only the Race (Elf), not the faction keyword. The bow/throwing/cavalry limits are 33.33% of the current models rounded up (BC: 'a third of the models'). A company of 7 with 4 Elves (57%) is accepted. OPTIONS: (A) keep (limit measured against the full 15-model company, never blocks early growth); (B) 33% of the current models after the new one joins, rounded down (strict: 6 models -> 1... with 3 of 7 allowed only at 9+ models); (C) as (B) but rounded up like the other limits. RECOMMENDATION: C for consistency with the other BC limits (6 models: 2 Elves; 9: 3; 12: 4). Helm's Deep starts with 2 Elves in 6 models, so B would already forbid the starting company.

title: Review: Fiefdoms promotion 'Knight of Dol Amroth on armoured horse' is priced 26 points (armoured horse 15) but the vanilla mounted Knight is 20
description: Fiefdoms advancement: Knight of Dol Amroth -> Knight of Dol Amroth on armoured horse. The json gives the promoted unit only wargear [Armoured horse]. The profile's vanilla options are 'Armoured horse and lance' 9 pts (and banner/war horn variants, not sold). A knight with [Armoured horse] matches no option, so it is charged the armoury rating of the horse (15): 11 + 15 = 26. A knight with [Armoured horse, Lance] matches the option: 11 + 9 = 20 (= the vanilla Knight of Dol Amroth on armoured horse). OPTIONS: (A) promotion gives wargear [Armoured horse, Lance]: 20 pts, matches the vanilla mounted knight, the rule text 'on armoured horse' reads as the mounted profile. (B) keep [Armoured horse] only: 26 pts, follows the armoury price table literally. RECOMMENDATION: A (data change in the advancement: wargear [Armoured horse, Lance]); curator edits, the app needs no change. Evidence: BC Fiefdoms 'Knight of Dol Amroth -> Knight of Dol Amroth on armoured horse'; vanilla Knight of Dol Amroth options. title: Casting value and range of every magical power (learned through paths)
description: For the curator. A hero on the Path of the Sorcerer learns Magical Powers (BC paths, rolls 3 and 10: 'Choice of Magical Power or improve an existing power's Casting Value by 1, max 2 improvements per power'). The unit card shows 'Black Dart 3+ . 12"' for each learned power. Vanilla's data.magicalPowers has only name, duration and definition; casting value and range exist only on the units that know a power natively (units[].magicalPowers: name, range, casting). Needed: the BASE casting value and range of each magical power (from the rulebook's Magical Powers table), so a learned power can be shown and improved (casting value - 1 per improvement, max 2). Put it in the Battle Companies JSON beside the other additions (e.g. data.magicalPowerStats) with validation that every vanilla power has an entry. Also say which powers a path may offer (the path text says 'Choice of Magical Power').
notes: Already satisfied by data.magicalPowers.items[] (range+casting for the 31 powers on the Sorcerer Spell List, schema requires them when learnable; paths offer items[learnable]). Added validator check: every vanilla power has an item, learnable == Spell List. REVIEW: the 12 non-learnable powers have no base value (vanilla units disagree per unit; paths cannot offer them); left without values rather than invent one.

title: Glossary page with search in the web app
description: A page listing the glossary terms (brief explanations, grouped by category) with a search bar (client-side filter with Alpine over the server-rendered list, matching name and aliases), deep-linkable per term. Later the same data feeds the help popups of the concept graph. Mobile first, see docs/frontend.md.
notes:
Design recommendation (not built, waiting for the owner's decision): the glossary belongs to the campaign's ruleset triple (vanilla, battle_companies, glossary) because BC resolves names against vanilla then glossary and rulesets are already identified by the hash of the triple (docs/definitions.md). Pin it per campaign at creation (default allowed, same picker as the other two files: static/js/ruleset_picker.js is generic over kind). The sidebar Glossary page browses the app default glossary, with 'use another glossary' (known by hash, or upload) remembered in a cookie like the other preferences (e.g. bcm-glossary=<hash>); inside a campaign a Glossary link shows that campaign's glossary. No forced first-login call to action. Page: client-side search over name+aliases (listSearch exists), deep links #term-id, show name/version of the active glossary. Linking is done by the backend at load time: build a name+alias index, find mentions in each term's text (longest match, skip self, once per hash, cached with the loader maps) and hand the page entry text as segments [{text}|{term: id, text}] so the template never renders raw HTML. The JSON stays untouched. Wait for the curator's glossary restructure (6lu.8) before building: entries, aliases and see-links are changing.
Built on the fake: campaign Glossary tab and the sidebar Glossary (default file), core.BuildGlossary (linking by name/alias, whole words, first mention per definition), client-side search over name+aliases, the glossary as the third rules file of a campaign (picker, Rules card). Backend work left: persist the campaign's glossary hash, load/link once per hash with the loader maps (x8p), and optionally remember a 'browse with another glossary' choice in a cookie for the sidebar page. Tuning ideas: many links are noise for ordinary words (Will, Move, Turn): consider case-sensitive matching for single common words or an explicit link list in the file; add a category filter.
SPEC DONE (remaining work): docs/frontend.md Glossary (last paragraph). Beads 2p6.1 (backend, case-sensitive single words, ByHash), 2p6.2 (category filter, name/version), 2p6.3 (another glossary + bcm-glossary cookie; needs 7v5.12). REVIEW: category filter in the URL (?c=); single-word case rule as default. The glossary-per-campaign pinning and 'backend persists the glossary hash' are covered by 7v5.12/7v5.14.

title: Review: promotion rows 'X' and 'X with <gear>' both apply to a unit carrying the gear (Muster of Isengard, Hill Tribes, Sharkey's Rogues, Westfold)
description:
BC advancement tables list a general row and gear-specific rows, e.g. Muster of Isengard: 'Scout -> Warrior with pike', 'Scout with shield -> Warrior with shield', 'Scout with Uruk bow -> Warrior with crossbow'; Sharkey's: 'Hill Tribesman -> Traitor', 'Hill Tribesman with spear -> Traitor with Shield & Throwing Spear', 'Hill Tribesman -> Traitor with Shield'. Advancement.Matches treats an empty FromWargear row as matching any unit of that profile, so a Scout with a shield (or a Tribesman with a bow) may be promoted by either the general row or the specific one; the specific row is not exclusive.
Reading A (current): general rows are open to every carrier; specific rows only add options. Reading B: a unit carrying the gear of a specific row can only take that row (a shield Scout becomes the shield Warrior, never the pike Warrior), the general row is for units with none of the listed gear.
Recommendation: A (the rulebook never says a promotion removes a choice); no change made. Fixed in passing: FromWargear compared names instead of item identity, so 'Uruk bow' never matched an Uruk-Hai Bow (Scout with bow could not become a crossbow Warrior).
close_reason: User: player chooses the promotion when several options exist; verified in the picker (pib.34)
